Its shape resembles Pratt’s primality certificates, but its role is to determine orders and transition probabilities. Prime labels are checked by an exact deterministic primality procedure based on the Agrawal–Kayal–Saxena polynomial-congruence method.

Ordinary transitions are mixed with uniform guesses, and filters computed from completed data make every accepted transition retain the same exact mass. A key logical point is that the deferred tests mark exactly the same recorded runs as a hypothetical sequence using true data from the start. Passing those tests itself forces the run to generate the required data. Thus the analysis does not smuggle that information into the algorithm as advice.

Keep all branches, then amplify

Adaptive classical choices can be simulated reversibly. Instead of measuring and forgetting a history, the circuit copies the intended basis outcomes into history qubits and uses them as controls. Different histories remain orthogonal. A fixed polynomial clock and retained work registers allow the entire preparation and its inverse to be compiled uniformly.

A further dyadic correction makes the preparation’s complete-success probability exactly 1/41/41/4. The established pair of sign reflections then gives probability one after a single amplification iteration. Boolean success predicates and reflections are implemented exactly using the stated finite gates.

Retaining unsuccessful branches is essential. Renormalizing a selected branch without paying its probability would amount to postselection and would describe a different computational model.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The result is an ideal exact-circuit statement. Physical gate noise and approximate implementations are outside that mathematical guarantee. Replacing a specified gate by an approximation does not preserve literal probability-one success.

The theorem supplies polynomial upper bounds, not competitive practical resource estimates. It makes no claim of deterministic classical polynomial-time factoring, nor does it automatically extend to every order-finding or discrete-logarithm formulation without checking their inputs and gate requirements.

The auxiliary data and exact probability calculations are central to the construction. Whether similar techniques can produce simpler exact algorithms or improve resource exponents is a further question. The current claim is the combination of certainty, uniformity, a fixed finite gate set and polynomial worst-case bounds.

8. Sources and further reading

Shor’s algorithm and Mosca–Zalka’s exact-transform work are linked above. For the amplification framework, see Brassard, Høyer, Mosca and Tapp, Quantum amplitude amplification and estimation. The source below gives the prescribed-probability order trial, deferred tests and exact circuit construction, reported as stated.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set (September 25, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Two languages for conformal field theory, with matching particles and fusion
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 280 · Mathematical physics
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

One mathematical description of a quantum field theory begins with formal series of field operators and their algebraic identities. Another begins with algebras of bounded observables assigned to spatial regions. They are intended to describe the same local physics, but translating between them requires more than matching symbols.

Family 280 concerns chiral conformal field theory, describing one directional component of a two-dimensional conformal theory, often formulated on a circle. Its two languages are vertex operator algebras, or VOAs, and conformal nets.

The manuscript claims a full comparison for simple unitary strongly rational VOAs. It constructs the associated local net, establishes positivity for every simple module and its fusion products, and identifies the representation theories with their fusion and braiding. An extension correspondence then follows through Gui’s existing comparison theorems.

2. Background and essential definitions

Formal fields and energy levels

A VOA is a complex vector space VVV with a vacuum vector Ω\OmegaΩ, a conformal vector determining symmetry and energy, and a field attached to each state:

Y(a,z)=∑n∈Za(n)z−n−1.Y(a,z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}a_{(n)}z^{-n-1}.Y(a,z)=n∈Z∑​a(n)​z−n−1.

The coefficients a(n)a_{(n)}a(n)​ are linear operators called modes. The variable zzz is initially formal; algebraic identities encode how fields combine and commute. The conformal energy operator L0L_0L0​ grades the space.

The theorem requires CFT type, meaning

V=⨁n≥0Vn,V0=CΩ.V=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V_n,\qquad V_0=\mathbb C\Omega.V=n≥0⨁​Vn​,V0​=CΩ.

Thus vacuum energy is zero and its space is one dimensional. “Simple” excludes nontrivial ideals preserved by the field operations. “Unitary” supplies a positive invariant Hermitian inner product, normalized on the vacuum, and the corresponding conjugation operation. Completing this inner-product space produces a Hilbert space.

Strong rationality combines several algebraic conditions. Besides CFT type and identification with the graded dual representation, it requires complete reducibility of admissible modules and finite dimension of

V/C2(V),C2(V)=span⁡{a(−2)b:a,b∈V}.V/C_2(V),\qquad C_2(V)=\operatorname{span}\{a_{(-2)}b:a,b\in V\}.V/C2​(V),C2​(V)=span{a(−2)​b:a,b∈V}.

The latter condition is a finiteness constraint on how much independent structure remains after certain field products are removed. These hypotheses give a controlled, finite representation theory; they are substantially stronger than unitarity alone.

Local observable algebras

A conformal net assigns a von Neumann algebra A(I)\mathcal A(I)A(I) to each proper open interval III of the circle. A von Neumann algebra is an algebra of bounded Hilbert-space operators closed under adjoints and weak operator limits. The assignments respect inclusion, conformal symmetry and locality: observables in disjoint intervals commute.

To pass from a formal field to an operator, smear it against a smooth function supported in an interval. Polynomial energy bounds control its modes, schematically

∥a(n)b∥≤C(1+∣n∣)p∥(1+L0)kb∥.\|a_{(n)}b\|\leq C(1+|n|)^p\|(1+L_0)^k b\|.∥a(n)​b∥≤C(1+∣n∣)p∥(1+L0​)kb∥.

These bounds allow closed smeared operators to be defined. Strong locality requires their generated bounded operator algebras to commute for disjoint supports. Formal commutation on a common domain alone does not guarantee this property for unbounded operators.

Modules, sectors and fusion

A VOA module is another space on which the same field identities act. The theorem uses finite-length, grading-restricted modules: they have finitely many simple constituents, finite-dimensional energy spaces and energies bounded below. A net representation, often called a sector, describes the local observable algebras acting on another Hilbert space.

Fusion combines two excitation types; it is not generally the ordinary vector-space tensor product. Braiding records the operation of exchanging them with the chosen orientation. A braided unitary tensor equivalence says the two descriptions match objects, maps, fusion, inner products and exchange operations coherently—not merely the number of particle types.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Carpi, Kawahigashi, Longo and Weiner developed the construction from strongly local unitary VOAs to conformal nets. They established major examples, including affine, Virasoro and moonshine theories, and conjectured strong locality for every simple unitary VOA. The present manuscript addresses that conjecture under the additional strong-rationality hypothesis.

Each representation theory already had substantial internal structure. Huang established rigidity and modularity for strongly rational VOA tensor categories. Kawahigashi, Longo and Müger established modularity for completely rational conformal nets. Having two modular categories does not itself identify them.

The Carpi–Weiner–Xu construction integrates unitary modules through their closed smeared fields. Gui developed tensor and braiding comparisons under appropriate charged-field hypotheses. Complete unitarity, equivalence and net rationality were already known for broad families: positive-integral-level affine and parafermion VOAs, positive-definite even lattice VOAs, certain discrete-series W-algebras, and further tensor products and cosets under stated conditions.

The analytic estimates also have direct predecessors. Carpi, Tanimoto and Weiner connected optimal energy orders of suitable generators to strong locality. Carpi and Tomassini used contraction estimates to improve exponential mode growth to polynomial growth. Wassermann’s loop-group work used bounded primary fields to calculate fusion. Gui and Tener developed transport forms and positivity methods for fusion products.

In the reverse direction, Henriques and Tener constructed VOAs and modules from conformal-net data under their stated energy and locality conventions. Their annulus and multidisc constructions supply geometric tools used here after locality has been established. The new claim is to derive the needed analytic and positivity conditions from strong rationality and unitarity, then show that no finite-index sector is missed.

4. What the new manuscript claims

For every simple unitary strongly rational complex VOA VVV, the manuscript states that polynomial energy bounds hold and the VOA is strongly local. The smeared fields therefore generate an irreducible conformal net AV\mathcal A_VAV​.

Every simple grading-restricted module is claimed to admit a positive invariant Hermitian form. Moreover, the canonical Hermitian forms on fusion products are positive definite. Together these properties are called complete unitarity. Positivity of the vacuum form is thus extended to the full module and fusion theory.

Every already unitary finite-length grading-restricted module is strongly integrable: its Hilbert completion carries compatible normal representations of the local algebras, and those representations reproduce the actual closed smeared fields, including their domains.

The net is claimed to be completely rational. This means irreducibility, the split property for separated intervals, strong additivity when an interior point is removed, and finiteness of the two-interval μ\muμ-index. The index measures the size of the inclusion of the two-interval observable algebra in the commutant of its complement; finiteness expresses a strong control on sectors.

After choosing invariant positive forms on simple modules, the canonical Carpi–Weiner–Xu functor gives

Rep⁡(V)≃Rep⁡u(V)≃Rep⁡f(AV).\operatorname{Rep}(V)\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_u(V)\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_f(\mathcal A_V).Rep(V)≃Repu​(V)≃Repf​(AV​).

The right-hand category consists of finite-index locally normal sectors and finite sums; its fusion is Connes fusion and its braiding is the Doplicher–Haag–Roberts braiding. The equivalence is braided, unitary and tensorial with a common circle orientation.

Finally, using Gui’s extension theorems, the manuscript obtains a correspondence between normalized CFT-type unitary extensions of VVV with finite-length underlying VVV-module and normalized irreducible finite-index local extensions of AV\mathcal A_VAV​. The embeddings preserve vacuum and conformal structure, with specified isometric vacuum embeddings. Equivalently, the algebraic side consists of simple CFT-type extensions with the same conformal vector, equipped with the asserted unique compatible unitary structure. These normalization and finiteness conditions belong to the statement.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5, provisional. The family claims a general bridge between two major mathematical formulations of rational unitary chiral conformal field theory. It goes beyond constructing a vacuum net by matching the full finite representation theory and extension structure.

Such a bridge allows algebraic information about modules and fusion to be interpreted as operator-algebraic information about localized sectors, and conversely. The positivity assertions also remove a potential obstruction: an algebraic representation need not come with a physically suitable Hilbert-space inner product merely because the vacuum does.

The significance is within the stated rational unitary class. The result is not advertised as a correspondence for every conformal field theory. Its score reflects the scope and structural consequences if the claims hold, without independent proof verification.

6. The main idea

Construct locality before using net geometry

Finite-dimensionality of V/C2(V)V/C_2(V)V/C2​(V) supplies a finite generating filtration. Positivity of zero modes gives an initial growth estimate. Two contraction arguments then improve it first to polynomial bounds and then to the optimal energy order needed by the existing locality criterion.

This order of construction matters. Annulus methods presuppose a net, so they enter only after the analytic locality problem has been addressed. The manuscript does not use a hoped-for net to justify its own existence.

Transfer positivity through local fields

For modules already carrying positive forms, annulus estimates control creation fields, which insert a charged state into the vacuum. Their bounded regularizations and sufficiently large ranges yield normal actions of the local observable algebras on module completions.

Creation operators then form positive Gram matrices in the vacuum algebra. The newly constructed normal representations transfer those matrices to other unitary modules. Algebraic rigidity supplies a nondegenerate fusion form, and energy-by-energy moment arguments establish its positivity. This produces positive fusion before assuming that every module is unitary.

Reach all modules and all sectors

To unitarize a remaining simple module PPP, the manuscript studies the flip symmetry of V⊗VV\otimes VV⊗V. A unitary twisted construction from the vacuum detects constituents of P⊗P∨P\otimes P^\veeP⊗P∨ inside a positive fusion product, where P∨P^\veeP∨ is the graded dual module. Combining invariant forms extends positivity to the full tensor-product algebra, and restriction gives a positive form on PPP.

The charged-field estimates now permit Gui’s braided tensor embedding. Surjectivity requires another step: starting from an arbitrary irreducible locally normal sector, the manuscript uses reconstruction and algebraic regularity to find an ordinary simple VOA module inside it. A reducing-projection argument identifies the whole sector with that module. Finiteness of the resulting sector list and existing operator-algebraic criteria then yield complete rationality.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

Strong rationality and unitarity are both essential hypotheses of the reported theorem. Nonrational theories, logarithmic nonsemisimple representation categories and general nonunitary VOAs are outside its scope. The wider strong-locality conjecture for every simple unitary VOA is not fully resolved by this restricted statement.

The comparison concerns grading-restricted finite-length modules and finite-index sectors, with specified Hilbert completions and closed-field domains. It is stronger than a formal identification of fusion rules but does not classify all strongly rational VOAs.

The extension corollary depends on existing comparison theorems and uses normalized finite-index local extensions. Other extension notions or different conformal vectors require separate treatment. These boundaries preserve the distinction between a broad correspondence theorem and an unrestricted equivalence of every possible formulation of conformal field theory.

8. Sources and further reading

The CKLW construction and Henriques–Tener reconstruction papers are linked above. Gui’s extension comparison supplies the extension framework. The source below states the new energy, positivity, integration and completeness claims and credits the tensor-category inputs used in their assembly.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Strongly rational unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets (September 25, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: A molecular density that no ordinary Kohn–Sham ensemble reproduces
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 278 · Mathematical physics
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

Density-functional theory replaces the full many-electron wavefunction with a simpler object: the electron density in ordinary three-dimensional space. Kohn–Sham theory then seeks a noninteracting system whose ground-state density matches that of the interacting electrons.

This raises an existence question. Given a density produced by a genuine Coulomb ground state, must some common local potential reproduce it using noninteracting electrons? Allowing mixtures of degenerate ground states makes the question more permissive than asking for one chosen orbital configuration.

Family 278 reports a counterexample: a finite three-electron molecule with two equal positive integer nuclear charges. Its spin-summed ground-state density is claimed to have no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation in the potential class L3/2(R3)+L∞(R3)L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)L3/2(R3)+L∞(R3). The mechanism involves a small but persistent density tail on a symmetry plane and an obstruction applying to every possible ground-state ensemble.

2. Background and essential definitions

Density is less information than a wavefunction

A three-electron wavefunction depends on three positions and three spin labels and is antisymmetric under exchange of two electrons. Its spin-summed density nΨ(r)n_\Psi(r)nΨ​(r) is obtained by integrating the squared wavefunction over the other positions and summing spins. It satisfies

nΨ(r)≥0,∫R3nΨ(r) dr=3.n_\Psi(r)\geq0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}n_\Psi(r)\,dr=3.nΨ​(r)≥0,∫R3​nΨ​(r)dr=3.

The density records the expected number of electrons per unit volume. It does not retain all correlations between their positions.

A noninteracting comparison system uses one scalar potential vvv for every electron and both spin components:

Hs(v)=∑i=13(−12Δi+v(ri)).H_s(v)=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\left(-\frac12\Delta_i+v(r_i)\right).Hs​(v)=i=1∑3​(−21​Δi​+v(ri​)).

“Local” means that vvv acts by multiplication at a position, rather than coupling different positions through an integral operator. The admissible real potential space is

V=L3/2(R3;R)+L∞(R3;R).\mathcal V=L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R).V=L3/2(R3;R)+L∞(R3;R).

Thus v=v1+v2v=v_1+v_2v=v1​+v2​, where ∫∣v1∣3/2<∞\int|v_1|^{3/2}<\infty∫∣v1​∣3/2<∞ and v2v_2v2​ is essentially bounded. This accommodates ordinary Coulomb singularities: near a nucleus 1/∣r∣1/|r|1/∣r∣ belongs locally to L3/2L^{3/2}L3/2, while its far-away portion is bounded.

Representation by a ground-state ensemble

A ground-state ensemble is a positive trace-one operator Γ\GammaΓ supported in the eigenspace at the bottom of Hs(v)H_s(v)Hs​(v). It can mix several degenerate ground states. Its density nΓn_\GammanΓ​ is the corresponding average density.

The target property is nΓ=nΨn_\Gamma=n_\PsinΓ​=nΨ​ almost everywhere. All complex spinful states and arbitrary ground-space degeneracy are allowed. Merely finding orbitals whose squared magnitudes add to the desired density is insufficient: those orbitals must arise from ground states of one common local potential.

A Slater determinant is the antisymmetrized product of occupied spin-orbitals. Noninteracting ground states can be described through such occupations, but allowing ensembles introduces more freedom than a single determinant ansatz. The claimed counterexample must rule out that extra freedom too.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Hohenberg and Kohn established the density-functional viewpoint. Their density–potential uniqueness principle and existence of a noninteracting representing potential are separate questions. Kohn and Sham introduced the effective noninteracting construction that became central to electronic-structure calculations.

Levy’s and Lieb’s constrained-search formulations distinguish densities produced by admissible states from densities selected as ground states by a potential. Ullrich and Kohn emphasized how ground-state ensembles enlarge the latter class. Consequently failure of one guessed determinant does not establish failure of ensemble representation.

Earlier counterexamples could be specified directly as densities. Wagner and collaborators discuss a positive two-electron density with finite kinetic energy whose cusp forces an inverse potential outside the usual potential class. That construction does not itself make the density the ground-state density of a finite Coulomb molecule.

Trushin, Erhard and Görling reported numerical indications of noninteracting representability failures through atomic density inversion. Other work studied open-shell symmetry constraints. These are relevant predecessors, but the present manuscript claims an analytic exclusion for every ground-state ensemble of a specified interacting Coulomb system.

Positive results also depend on setting. Chayes, Chayes and Ruskai studied lattice systems. Corso treated spinless fermions on a bounded one-dimensional interval, while Sutter and collaborators obtained ensemble representation on a one-dimensional torus. Their hypotheses, including distributional potentials in the latter continuum settings, differ from three-dimensional Coulomb densities in V\mathcal VV.

The asymptotic idea has a particularly direct predecessor. Gori-Giorgi, Gál and Baerends analyzed how a nodal plane in a leading electron-removal amplitude can force unusual density tails and difficult Kohn–Sham potential behavior. Gori-Giorgi and Baerends later studied related effective density equations. The manuscript builds on that mechanism and adds a finite Coulomb construction, an all-ensemble kinetic certificate and an exclusion of the entire sum space V\mathcal VV.

4. What the new manuscript claims

The molecule has three electrons and two nuclei of equal charge ZZZ, located at ±(D/Z)ez\pm(D/Z)e_z±(D/Z)ez​, where ez=(0,0,1)e_z=(0,0,1)ez​=(0,0,1) and the manuscript fixes D=10200D=10^{200}D=10200. Its electronic Hamiltonian is

HC=∑i=13(−12Δi−Z∣ri−(D/Z)ez∣−Z∣ri+(D/Z)ez∣)+∑1≤i<j≤31∣ri−rj∣.\begin{aligned}H_C={}&\sum_{i=1}^{3}\left(-\frac12\Delta_i-\frac Z{|r_i-(D/Z)e_z|}-\frac Z{|r_i+(D/Z)e_z|}\right)\\&+\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq3}\frac1{|r_i-r_j|}.\end{aligned}HC​=​i=1∑3​(−21​Δi​−∣ri​−(D/Z)ez​∣Z​−∣ri​+(D/Z)ez​∣Z​)+1≤i<j≤3∑​∣ri​−rj​∣1​.​

The manuscript specifies a finite positive integer ZZZ by an exact nonnumerical formula in its equation (7.10). It uses auxiliary spectral data, densities and an angle minimization; it does not define the charge by searching over possible representing potentials. No effective numerical upper bound on ZZZ is asserted.

For this fixed finite system, the theorem claims a normalizable absolute ground state Ψ\PsiΨ in the sector Sz=1/2S_z=1/2Sz​=1/2, and states that no v∈Vv\in\mathcal Vv∈V and no ground-state ensemble Γ\GammaΓ of Hs(v)H_s(v)Hs​(v) satisfy nΓ=nΨn_\Gamma=n_\PsinΓ​=nΨ​ almost everywhere. The original state is an absolute ground state, not merely a state minimizing energy within an artificially selected spin sector.

A functional consequence concerns the noninteracting kinetic constrained search Tens[n]T_{\mathrm{ens}}[n]Tens​[n] and the interacting internal-energy search Fens[n]F_{\mathrm{ens}}[n]Fens​[n]. Define

EHxc[n]=Fens[n]−Tens[n].E_{\mathrm{Hxc}}[n]=F_{\mathrm{ens}}[n]-T_{\mathrm{ens}}[n].EHxc​[n]=Fens​[n]−Tens​[n].

This is the ensemble Hartree–exchange–correlation functional. At the constructed density, the manuscript excludes a local potential w∈Vw\in\mathcal Vw∈V representing its one-sided first variation along every segment to every density in the common finite-energy domain. It also states that TensT_{\mathrm{ens}}Tens​ has no V\mathcal VV-valued subgradient there. A subgradient is a linear supporting functional lying below a convex functional at every competing density.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5, provisional. The claimed example addresses an existence assumption underlying a central exact formulation of Kohn–Sham theory, while using a genuine finite Coulomb ground-state density and allowing all ground-state ensembles.

The distinction from a prescribed artificial density is significant. It would show that the representability obstruction can arise within the interacting molecular problem itself. The ensemble quantifier also prevents degeneracy and fractional occupations from automatically repairing the example.

This is an existence boundary, not a judgment on the practical success of approximate density-functional calculations. The molecule uses an exceptionally chosen charge and geometry, and the theorem excludes a specified potential class. The score concerns the conceptual significance if the claims hold, without independently assessing the proof.

6. The main idea

Make interaction weak after rescaling

Rescale positions by y=Zry=Zry=Zr and divide energy by Z2Z^2Z2. The two nuclear charges become one, their half-separation becomes DDD, and electron repulsion has coefficient λ=1/Z\lambda=1/Zλ=1/Z.

The two lowest one-particle orbitals are an even positive orbital bbb and an odd orbital eee, whose sign changes across the median plane. At zero interaction the three electrons occupy bbb with both spins and eee with one spin. The manuscript follows this state to small positive interaction.

An electron-removal amplitude describes what remains when one electron is separated from the two-electron ion. The leading amplitude has an odd angular zero on the median plane. Coupling to other ionic channels produces a smaller nonzero planar tail. Its exponential decay rate matches the leading off-plane rate, but it carries an additional inverse power of distance. The nonzero coefficient is essential: a vanished tail would not create the obstruction.

Certify the best noninteracting kinetic representation

For the scaled density nnn, the manuscript minimizes a weighted angle energy ∫n∣∇θ∣2\int n|\nabla\theta|^2∫n∣∇θ∣2, with ∫nsin⁡2θ=1\int n\sin^2\theta=1∫nsin2θ=1 and an odd reflection condition on θ\thetaθ. Set

g=ncos⁡θ,h=nsin⁡θ.g=\sqrt n\cos\theta,\qquad h=\sqrt n\sin\theta.g=n​cosθ,h=n​sinθ.

Their squared norms are two and one. They encode a doubly occupied spatial orbital and a singly occupied one. A weighted spectral estimate makes the resulting determinant a kinetic-energy minimum among all ensembles having density nnn.

That all-ensemble certificate is the bridge from one constructed pair of orbitals to every hypothetical representing potential. The manuscript concludes that any such local potential must equal Δg/(2g)\Delta g/(2g)Δg/(2g), up to an additive constant, and that g,hg,hg,h obey common potential equations with distinct orbital energies.

Compare the forced decay with the actual tail

Assume the forced potential belongs to V\mathcal VV. The manuscript translates bounded observation windows far out along the median plane and studies weak limits of the orbital equations. It derives an exterior energy bound forcing ggg to decay exponentially faster than the density’s known leading rate.

That improved decay also controls the trace of ggg on the plane. But oddness gives θ=0\theta=0θ=0 there, hence g=ng=\sqrt ng=n​. The nonzero interaction-induced planar tail decays too slowly to satisfy the improved exponential integrability. This contradiction excludes V\mathcal VV.

The argument uses weak potential limits and a Sobolev trace, rather than assuming pointwise convergence of a candidate potential at infinity. That is why the stated obstruction covers the full integrable-plus-bounded class.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The theorem concerns one common real, spin-independent local potential in L3/2+L∞L^{3/2}+L^\inftyL3/2+L∞. It makes no assertion about larger distributional classes, spin-dependent potentials or nonlocal one-particle operators. Enlarging the comparison class changes the representability question.

The charge is finitely specified but not numerically bounded effectively by the theorem. No claim is made that this is a typical molecule or that its geometry is physically stable when nuclear motion is allowed. The result is for the stated clamped Coulomb Hamiltonian.

The functional corollary excludes a local first variation valid along every admissible segment. It should not be paraphrased as failure of every possible directional derivative or every weaker differentiability notion. Identifying broad positive representability classes and physically informative versions of this obstruction remains a separate task.

8. Sources and further reading

The foundational Hohenberg–Kohn and Kohn–Sham papers and the nodal-plane predecessor are linked above. For the constrained-search distinction, see Lieb, Density functionals for Coulomb systems. The source below supplies the finite molecule, ensemble certificate and potential-class exclusion, reported as stated.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation (September 25, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: QAOA reaches the spin-glass optimum—when system size goes first
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 281 · Mathematical physics
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm, or QAOA, alternates two simple types of quantum evolution. One encodes an objective function; the other mixes possible answers. Increasing the number of alternating layers enlarges the family of states it can prepare.

For a fixed finite instance, sufficiently many layers can approach the optimum. A harder question asks whether, for each desired accuracy, one finite depth can work for arbitrarily large random instances. The depth must be chosen before sending the system size to infinity.

Family 281 reports this property for the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass. Its companion studies the full support of the zero-temperature Parisi order parameter, supplying one route to the classical near-optimal calculation that the QAOA construction compiles. The family concerns asymptotic attainability; it does not provide an efficient angle-selection algorithm or a quantitative depth bound.

2. Background and essential definitions

A random optimization landscape

For nnn signs σi∈{−1,1}\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}σi​∈{−1,1}, define

hn,J(σ)=1n∑i<jJijσiσj,h_{n,J}(\sigma)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j,hn,J​(σ)=n​1​i<j∑​Jij​σi​σj​,

where the JijJ_{ij}Jij​ are independent standard real Gaussian variables. Some pairs prefer equal signs and others opposite signs, creating frustration. The normalization makes the optimal energy of order nnn.

The positive optimum per spin is

P∗=lim⁡n→∞1nEmax⁡σhn,J(σ).P_* =\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\mathbb E\max_\sigma h_{n,J}(\sigma).P∗​=n→∞lim​n1​Eσmax​hn,J​(σ).

The manuscript maximizes this sign convention; equivalently it studies the ground energy of its negative. The expectation averages over the random couplings.

For quantum spins, replace σi\sigma_iσi​ by the Pauli matrix ZiZ_iZi​, giving the cost operator Cn,JC_{n,J}Cn,J​, and use the mixer Bn=∑iXiB_n=\sum_iX_iBn​=∑i​Xi​. The initial state ∣+⟩⊗n|+\rangle^{\otimes n}∣+⟩⊗n is the uniform superposition of all sign configurations. A depth-ppp QAOA state is

∣ψ⟩=e−iβpBne−iγpCn,J⋯e−iβ1Bne−iγ1Cn,J∣+⟩⊗n.|\psi\rangle=e^{-i\beta_pB_n}e^{-i\gamma_pC_{n,J}}\cdots e^{-i\beta_1B_n}e^{-i\gamma_1C_{n,J}}|+\rangle^{\otimes n}.∣ψ⟩=e−iβp​Bn​e−iγp​Cn,J​⋯e−iβ1​Bn​e−iγ1​Cn,J​∣+⟩⊗n.

Measuring in the computational basis samples a classical configuration. Its expected objective equals ⟨ψ,Cn,Jψ⟩\langle\psi,C_{n,J}\psi\rangle⟨ψ,Cn,J​ψ⟩.

Overlaps and the Parisi description

The overlap of two configurations is R12=n−1∑iσi1σi2R_{12}=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_i^1\sigma_i^2R12​=n−1∑i​σi1​σi2​. It measures their similarity. The Parisi variational description uses an order parameter organizing overlap scales.

At zero temperature in covariance convention ξ(t)=t2/2\xi(t)=t^2/2ξ(t)=t2/2, the admissible order parameter is a nonnegative, nondecreasing, right-continuous function γ:[0,1)→[0,∞)\gamma:[0,1)\to[0,\infty)γ:[0,1)→[0,∞) with finite integral. This γ\gammaγ is a function, distinct from the QAOA angle vector of the same conventional name.

Its Stieltjes measure satisfies μγ([0,t])=γ(t)\mu_\gamma([0,t])=\gamma(t)μγ​([0,t])=γ(t), including a possible atom γ(0)\gamma(0)γ(0) at zero. It need not be a probability measure or have finite total mass. Full relative support means every nonempty open overlap interval below one carries positive measure.

The corresponding value function solves

∂tΦ=−12(∂xxΦ+γ(t)(∂xΦ)2),Φ(1,x)=∣x∣,\partial_t\Phi=-\frac12\bigl(\partial_{xx}\Phi+\gamma(t)(\partial_x\Phi)^2\bigr),\qquad \Phi(1,x)=|x|,∂t​Φ=−21​(∂xx​Φ+γ(t)(∂x​Φ)2),Φ(1,x)=∣x∣,

and the Parisi functional is P(γ)=Φ(0,0)−12∫01tγ(t) dt\mathcal P(\gamma)=\Phi(0,0)-\tfrac12\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dtP(γ)=Φ(0,0)−21​∫01​tγ(t)dt. Its minimum equals P∗P_*P∗​.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Sherrington and Kirkpatrick introduced the model, and Parisi proposed its hierarchical order parameter. Guerra established the interpolation bound and Talagrand the positive-temperature formula. Auffinger and Chen developed the zero-temperature formula and its attainment. Determining the minimizer’s support is a separate problem from proving the formula.

Auffinger, Chen and Zeng showed infinitely many zero-temperature support points. That does not exclude an interior interval containing none. More recently, Lopatto established full interval support in the low-temperature zero-field phase, and Hong-Bin Chen established zero-temperature full support and smooth absolute continuity. M2 explicitly credits this earlier full-support conclusion. Its contribution is a different coercive-identity argument, strict positivity of the density away from zero, and scalar consequences used in optimization.

Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann introduced QAOA. Later fixed-depth analysis of its SK performance established limiting formulas and concentration at fixed parameters. Basso, Farhi, Marwaha, Villalonga and Zhou related the limit to large-degree trees and conjectured eventual attainment of the Parisi value. Spin–boson calculations and semiclassical studies supplied further numerical and heuristic evidence.

Classical optimization supplies another key predecessor. Montanari’s Parisi-diffusion approach and the broader work of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke give near-optimal algorithms under support hypotheses. M1 compiles a finite classical calculation into standard QAOA controls. Its primary route uses M2; an independent positive-temperature route uses Lopatto’s support theorem and existing finite-iteration analysis.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

Eventual QAOA optimality

For fixed deterministic angles, define

vp(γ,β)=lim⁡n→∞1nE⟨ψ,Cn,Jψ⟩,Qp=sup⁡γ,βvp.v_p(\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\mathbb E\langle\psi,C_{n,J}\psi\rangle,\qquad Q_p=\sup_{\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta}v_p.vp​(γ,β)=n→∞lim​n1​E⟨ψ,Cn,J​ψ⟩,Qp​=γ,βsup​vp​.

M1 claims lim⁡p→∞Qp=P∗\lim_{p\to\infty}Q_p=P_*limp→∞​Qp​=P∗​. Precisely, for every ε>0\varepsilon>0ε>0, there exist a finite ppp and deterministic real angles, independent of both nnn and JJJ, with limiting expected energy at least P∗−εP_*-\varepsilonP∗​−ε.

The chosen word may contain inverse gates, zero angles and very large angles. It uses only the standard cost and transverse-field mixer in its final form. The theorem gives no quantitative finite-size rate, required-depth bound or efficient angle-selection procedure. It is stated in expected energy.

Full zero-temperature support

M2 claims that every admissible minimizer satisfies

supp⁡μγ=[0,1).\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1).suppμγ​=[0,1).

It obtains smoothness on [0,1)[0,1)[0,1), γ(0)=0\gamma(0)=0γ(0)=0 and γ′(t)>0\gamma'(t)>0γ′(t)>0 for 0<t<10<t<10<t<1. Thus the measure has a smooth density strictly positive away from zero. These statements concern the relative interval below one, not a claim of finite total mass or smooth extension through the endpoint one.

For the controlled diffusion dXt=γ(t)Φx(t,Xt) dt+dBtdX_t=\gamma(t)\Phi_x(t,X_t)\,dt+dB_tdXt​=γ(t)Φx​(t,Xt​)dt+dBt​, with X0=0X_0=0X0​=0 and standard Brownian motion BtB_tBt​, M2 also obtains consistency identities EΦx(t,Xt)2=t\mathbb E\Phi_x(t,X_t)^2=tEΦx​(t,Xt​)2=t and EΦxx(t,Xt)2=1\mathbb E\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t)^2=1EΦxx​(t,Xt​)2=1.

Applying the existing El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke theorem, M2 derives a randomized classical algorithm using at most C(ε)n2C(\varepsilon)n^2C(ε)n2 real-arithmetic operations and returning energy within εn\varepsilon nεn of the optimum with probability tending to one. Probability includes disorder and algorithmic randomness. This operation model should not be silently replaced by a bit-complexity claim.

A MaxCut consequence

M1 transfers the QAOA construction to large-degree regular graphs. For every η>0\eta>0η>0, it chooses a finite depth and normalized angles independent of degree and graph. For sufficiently large DDD, every simple unweighted (D+1)(D+1)(D+1)-regular graph of girth greater than 2p+12p+12p+1 has expected cut fraction at least

12+P∗−ηD,\frac12+\frac{P_*-\eta}{\sqrt D},21​+D​P∗​−η​,

using ordinary MaxCut cost angles scaled as 2γ/D2\boldsymbol\gamma/\sqrt D2γ/D​. Girth is the length of the shortest cycle. A random-regular-graph corollary makes the difference from the optimal cut negligible at the 1/D1/\sqrt D1/D​ scale, taking graph size to infinity first at fixed degree and then degree to infinity. The probability there is over the graph; the cut fraction already averages quantum measurement.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5, provisional. The family claims a central asymptotic attainability result for QAOA on a canonical spin glass, together with a structural analysis of the order parameter feeding the construction.

The limit order makes the result stronger than fixed-instance convergence as depth grows. One finite circuit word is chosen for an accuracy target and then used throughout the thermodynamic limit. At the same time, absent depth and angle-selection bounds prevent this from being an efficient practical optimization guarantee.

The classical near-optimal calculation also makes clear that this is not a demonstrated quantum speedup over classical algorithms. Its significance is that standard QAOA controls can asymptotically realize the required performance. The rating measures that claim if correct, while crediting the earlier support and optimization results.

6. The main idea

Exclude gaps in overlap support

M2 studies q(t)=EΦx(t,Xt)2q(t)=\mathbb E\Phi_x(t,X_t)^2q(t)=EΦx​(t,Xt​)2. Variational optimality supplies contact conditions at support points. On a hypothetical interval where the order parameter is a positive constant, an integrated rational identity gives strict convexity of q′q'q′.

The endpoint contact conditions force q′q'q′ to have average one across the interval, while strict convexity and endpoint bounds force it below one inside. This contradiction excludes an interior gap. Initial and terminal gaps require separate arguments. Once consistency holds at every time, derivative-moment identities yield smoothness and the stated positive density.

Compile a classical near-optimal formula

M1 first represents a bounded near-optimal calculation as a finite function of Gaussian variables on a rooted-tree Hilbert space. Normalized sums of child calculations supply new Gaussian coordinates. Smooth approximations and exclusions of selected vertex types prevent compiled operations from feeding back into their own controls.

Temporary longitudinal seed fields make the desired functions implementable through cost and mixer commutators. Small reserved sets of helper spins realize neighbor sums. The construction controls their contribution to energy rather than treating them as free extra resources.

Remove temporary controls before taking the limit

A further echo construction removes the longitudinal seed controls from the already selected finite circuit. Selective rotations and a large displacement produce the required effective field, while a separate energy calculation preserves the target value.

Only after all approximations and control removal does the argument choose one finite ordinary cost–mixer word and invoke the fixed-word tree-to-SK identity. This order prevents an auxiliary control or a system-size-dependent circuit from remaining hidden in the final QAOA claim.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

Both manuscripts concern the pure Gaussian zero-field SK model with the stated normalization. Nonzero external fields and general mixed-spin covariances are not included automatically.

M1 supplies existential depth and angles for limiting expected energy. It gives no explicit accuracy-depth law, efficient search procedure, finite-size guarantee or joint limit in which depth grows with nnn. Large angles may also carry implementation costs not measured by the layer count.

M2’s support result is not the first full-support statement; its distinct argument and scalar consequences should be assessed in that historical context. Quantitative QAOA bounds and extensions to other disordered optimization models remain separate questions beyond this family.

8. Sources and further reading

The Basso and collaborators paper states the QAOA conjecture and tree relation. Chen’s paper gives the earlier zero-temperature full-support result, and El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke provide the optimization theorem. M1 and M2 below specify the new constructions and their dependencies, reported as stated.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, QAOA attains the SK ground-state energy in the thermodynamic-first limit (September 25, 2026).
  • M2. OpenAI, Full support of the zero-temperature Sherrington-Kirkpatrick order parameter (September 27, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: When scale symmetry becomes local conformal symmetry in four dimensions
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 282 · Mathematical physics
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

A scale-invariant theory looks the same when all lengths are enlarged by a common factor. Conformal symmetry is stronger: it also permits position-dependent changes of scale that preserve angles locally. Why should uniform rescaling force this larger symmetry?

In quantum field theory, the answer depends on which local fields and observables belong to the theory. A formal transformation or a useful two-point function does not automatically produce a physical local operator with well-defined products.

Family 282 claims that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for a specified class of four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories. The central construction improves the stress tensor to make its trace vanish while preserving translation and Lorentz charges. Its conclusion is a local action through Ward identities. Integrating that action into a global conformal symmetry of the entire bounded observable net remains a separate question.

2. Background and essential definitions

Currents and the trace obstruction

Work in four-dimensional spacetime with metric η=diag⁡(1,−1,−1,−1)\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)η=diag(1,−1,−1,−1). The stress tensor TμνT_{\mu u}Tμν​ describes energy and momentum. It is symmetric and conserved: ∂μTμν=0\partial^\mu T_{\mu u}=0∂μTμν​=0. Integrating suitable components across a time slice gives translation and Lorentz generators.

A conserved dilation current has the form

Dμ=xνTμν−Vμ,Tμμ=∂μVμ.D_\mu=x^ u T_{\mu u}-V_\mu,\qquad T^\mu{}_{\mu}=\partial^\mu V_\mu.Dμ​=xνTμν​−Vμ​,Tμμ​=∂μVμ​.

The local vector field VμV_\muVμ​ is the virial field. The second identity follows from conservation of DμD_\muDμ​. Scale invariance therefore permits a nonzero stress-tensor trace if it is a divergence.

An improvement adds derivatives of local fields to the stress tensor without changing its physical charges. If a local scalar LLL satisfies Tμμ=□LT^\mu{}_{\mu}=\Box LTμμ​=□L, where □=∂μ∂μ\Box=\partial^\mu\partial_\mu□=∂μ∂μ​, then in four dimensions

tμν=Tμν+13(∂μ∂ν−ημν□)Lt_{\mu u}=T_{\mu u}+ rac13(\partial_\mu\partial_ u-\eta_{\mu u}\Box)Ltμν​=Tμν​+31​(∂μ​∂ν​−ημν​□)L

is conserved and traceless. The challenge is not this algebraic calculation; it is establishing that a suitable LLL actually belongs to the physical local theory.

Local Ward identities

A conformal Killing vector XXX generates an infinitesimal spacetime transformation whose metric change is proportional to the metric. For a symmetric conserved traceless tensor, the corresponding current is jμ=Xνtμνj_\mu=X^ u t_{\mu u}jμ​=Xνtμν​.

A Ward identity describes how the flux of that current around a field insertion generates its symmetry transformation. “Unbroken” means the vacuum and correlation functions satisfy the corresponding symmetry identities. Local Ward identities concern compact regions and insertions; they do not by themselves construct globally defined group transformations on every bounded observable.

Fields and bounded local operations

Point fields are distributions: they become operators after smearing with smooth test functions. These operators are often unbounded, so their domains matter. A bounded local net assigns a weakly closed operator algebra M(O)\mathcal M(O)M(O) to each spacetime region OOO, with commuting algebras at spacelike separation, or the appropriate statistics twist for fermions.

A closed field operator is affiliated with a local algebra when its spectral or graph data are controlled by that algebra. This ties the unbounded field to the bounded local operations. Weak commutation of fields on a small domain does not automatically establish the stronger bounded-algebra locality used in this manuscript.

3. Development history and previous partial results

In two dimensions, Zamolodchikov’s ccc-theorem and Polchinski’s enhancement result established a powerful route from scale to conformal symmetry under suitable assumptions. Four dimensions require different arguments.

Callan, Coleman and Jackiw developed the improved energy-momentum tensor. Perturbative local renormalization-group identities later gave substantial scale-to-conformal results. Flavor-current contributions matter: a cycle in ordinary beta functions need not describe a nonconformal physical theory. Extending perturbative positivity to arbitrary coupling is another issue.

Komargodski and Schwimmer’s four-dimensional aaa-theorem uses anomaly matching and a positive dilaton dispersion relation between conformal endpoints. Luty, Polchinski and Rattazzi developed this approach to constrain possible asymptotic theories and establish conformal behavior in perturbatively controlled regimes. Dymarsky, Komargodski, Schwimmer and Theisen sharpened the vanishing-amplitude argument.

A remaining distinction is between on-shell probe scattering and an off-shell local operator identity. Contact and semi-local terms can survive when scattering amplitudes vanish. Bzowski and Skenderis emphasized their role in carrying scale anomalies, while work on generalized-free traces isolated further alternatives rather than eliminating every improvement problem.

Yonekura proposed constructing a scalar by applying an inverse wave operator to the trace, with locality relying on stated analyticity and crossing assumptions. Sachs treated a restricted class of metric-couplable Lagrangian theories. The present manuscript aims to reconstruct the scalar within a prescribed physical net, without importing an independent scattering or crossing hypothesis.

Its modular methods also have predecessors. Faulkner, Leigh, Parrikar and Wang related deformations of half-space modular Hamiltonians to horizon stress integrals; Casini, Testé and Torroba developed null-plane modular relations. The new manuscript supplies the specific flux limits, domains and reconstruction statements it uses under its operational assumptions.

4. What the new manuscript claims

The theorem assumes a unitary, positive-energy theory on R1,3\mathbb R^{1,3}R1,3, with a Poincaré- and continuously scale-invariant vacuum. Original fields and adjoints generate the Hilbert space and obey Wightman distribution, covariance, spectrum and locality conditions on compatible invariant domains. Uniqueness of the invariant vacuum vector is not assumed.

Scaling dimensions form a real discrete spectrum, bounded below, with no finite accumulation and finite multiplicities after Lorentz components are counted. Every original field is a finite sum of homogeneous scaling fields. Infinite sums of scaling components are not silently admitted as new field labels.

The theory includes a fixed covariant causally commuting bounded local net. Original fields and adjoints have compatible closed affiliated realizations in that same net. A physical stress tensor and virial field obey local flux Ward identities, and the physical dilation current generates the stated scale transformations.

New fields can be admitted only after establishing arbitrarily sharp localization, every finite mixed product with original fields and adjoints, a compatible common invariant domain containing the original vacuum-word domain, and affiliation in the original net. This is an admission criterion, not an assumption that the desired scalar already exists.

Under these hypotheses, the manuscript selects the Hermitian dimension-four stress component T(4)T^{(4)}T(4) and dimension-three virial component V(3)V^{(3)}V(3), preserving the affine Ward charges, and constructs a Hermitian physical scalar LLL of dimension two such that

∂μVμ(3)=□L,tμν=Tμν(4)+13(∂μ∂ν−ημν□)L.\partial^\mu V_\mu^{(3)}=\Box L,\qquad t_{\mu u}=T_{\mu u}^{(4)}+ rac13(\partial_\mu\partial_ u-\eta_{\mu u}\Box)L.∂μVμ(3)​=□L,tμν​=Tμν(4)​+31​(∂μ​∂ν​−ημν​□)L.

The improved tensor is symmetric, conserved and traceless, with unchanged translation and Lorentz charges. Its conformal currents satisfy unbroken local Ward identities on the physical field algebra, extending the existing Poincaré and dilation actions.

The Hilbert space and bounded net are preserved. The common field domain is enlarged through reconstructed vacuum words, but the theorem does not identify every newly affiliated extension with every previously chosen closed operator on its larger domain.

The full massless free scalar theory supplies an example: its square field is available and gives the familiar stress improvement. Restricting to a shift-invariant field algebra can remove the needed virial current and square field. The local-current and intrinsic field-membership assumptions are therefore substantive.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5, provisional. The family addresses a central symmetry-enhancement problem while explicitly confronting the passage from correlation information to physical local operators. The claimed scalar is reconstructed in the original bounded net, rather than placed in an unspecified larger theory.

The distinction between local and global conclusions is equally important. A traceless stress tensor with conformal Ward identities gives detailed infinitesimal constraints on observables, but a global group action requires additional integration work. Preserving that boundary makes the theorem’s scope assessable.

The rating reflects the significance of the stated enhancement theorem if correct. It does not remove its operational hypotheses or independently verify the long analytic reconstruction.

6. The main idea

Extract information from null boundaries

Modular theory associates canonical operator flows with local algebras and a vacuum. The manuscript uses wedge modular data and inclusions associated with null cuts to obtain positive generators. A bounded-profile Ward identity identifies their response with physical stress-tensor flux.

Comparing two null horizons isolates a possible critical scalar tail. A dispersion comparison and logarithmic test force its positive leakage coefficient to vanish. This improves the scalar spectral estimate needed for the subsequent construction.

Distinguish a vacuum wave from a field

Applying a field to the vacuum gives a vector-valued distribution, or vacuum wave. Dividing trace polarization by invariant mass squared suggests a scalar wave, but that operation alone does not define a local field with arbitrary products.

The manuscript first identifies actual modular actions on time cones and local diamonds. These actions extract a dimension-two scalar wave from the virial field with real localization and bounded approximants in the original net. Short-product Ward identities and positivity on pair states then identify it with the trace-derived scalar wave.

Several actions play different roles: an auxiliary conformal action organizes two-point spectral comparisons, actual modular transformations act on the physical Hilbert space, and a pair-space conformal representation controls residual terms. They are not treated as interchangeable global symmetries.

Reconstruct all products before improving the tensor

Bounded approximants generate analytic products of every finite length. Differential identities, causal wave equations and controlled boundary limits establish the required distributions, spectral support and mixed orderings with original fields.

These products supply a common invariant domain with compatible adjoints. Commutation with the original bounded commutants establishes affiliation in the original local algebras. Only after this work does LLL become a physical field and the improvement formula become an operator identity with the claimed Ward action.

This reconstruction is the main conceptual burden: a correctly localized two-point object is only the beginning of a local quantum field.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The theorem is not an unconditional statement about every four-dimensional scale-invariant theory. Finite scaling support, the discrete finite-multiplicity dimension spectrum, compatible bounded locality and a physical local dilation current are explicit assumptions.

No Haag duality, split property, phase-space bound, scattering theory or a priori conformal action is assumed. That absence does not erase the assumptions that are present. In gauge descriptions, construction occurs in the chosen gauge-invariant local algebras.

The conclusion is local conformal Ward symmetry. Global conformal covariance of the whole bounded net remains open within the stated result. Other field classes, infinite scaling sums or differently chosen observable nets require separate analysis rather than an automatic application.

8. Sources and further reading

The improvement and dilaton papers linked above provide central predecessors. Polchinski’s Scale and conformal invariance in quantum field theory gives the earlier enhancement context. The source below states the operational hypotheses and local reconstruction theorem, whose claims are reported as stated.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory (September 26, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: A Boolean oracle for every quantum unitary
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 283 · Mathematical physics
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

An arbitrary operation on nnn qubits is a unitary matrix of dimension 2n2^n2n. Describing it usually requires exponentially many numbers. Suppose this description is stored behind a Boolean oracle that a quantum circuit can query coherently. Can a polynomial-size circuit use that access to perform the operation?

This question separates the size of stored information from the work required to use it. The oracle can be enormously complicated, but each query address, the workspace and the computation must remain polynomial in nnn.

Family 283 reports a positive answer to the constant-error version of the Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem. One circuit generated from nnn alone can approximate every nnn-qubit unitary after a suitable oracle is chosen. The oracle may depend on the target; the theorem does not efficiently construct it from a given matrix description.

2. Background and essential definitions

A classical function queried quantum mechanically

A Boolean function f:{0,1}m→{0,1}f:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}f:{0,1}m→{0,1} supplies the reversible gate

Of∣x,b⟩=∣x,b⊕f(x)⟩.O_f|x,b\rangle=|x,b\oplus f(x)\rangle.Of​∣x,b⟩=∣x,b⊕f(x)⟩.

Although its answers are bits, a query can use a superposition of addresses. The oracle then acts coherently on the entire superposition. This is more powerful than reading one classical table entry and forgetting its address.

The oracle’s input length is mmm, while its truth table has 2m2^m2m entries. Polynomial address length therefore permits an exponentially large table. Query complexity counts calls to OfO_fOf​; circuit complexity additionally counts ordinary gates and qubits. Small query count does not imply small query width or total resources.

A unitary UUU acts on states by the channel U(ρ)=UρU†\mathcal U(\rho)=U\rho U^\daggerU(ρ)=UρU†. The proposed circuit begins with zero workspace, retains nnn designated output qubits and discards the rest, producing a channel Φ\PhiΦ.

Error on every input, including entangled ones

The full diamond-norm error is

∥Φ−U∥⋄=sup⁡ρ∥((Φ−U)⊗id⁡R)(ρ)∥1.\|\Phi-\mathcal U\|_\diamond=\sup_\rho\|((\Phi-\mathcal U)\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\rho)\|_1.∥Φ−U∥⋄​=ρsup​∥((Φ−U)⊗idR​)(ρ)∥1​.

The supremum includes density matrices on the input and an nnn-qubit reference RRR. The trace norm is ∥X∥1=Tr⁡X†X\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{X^\dagger X}∥X∥1​=TrX†X​. This convention has no factor of one half; the maximum distance between channels is two.

Including a reference tests whether the circuit preserves correlations with systems it never touches. Agreement on a few basis inputs, or even preparation of each desired output column separately, would not establish this guarantee.

Uniform generation means a deterministic classical algorithm outputs the circuit in polynomial time from the input length. Its wiring and resource bounds cannot be redesigned separately for every target unitary; only the oracle changes.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Aaronson and Kuperberg posed the unitary synthesis question in their work on quantum and classical proofs and advice. Aaronson later highlighted it as an open problem in quantum query complexity.

State synthesis is an easier comparison problem: prepare one specified state from a fixed initial state. Irani, Natarajan, Nirkhe, Rao and Yuen obtained low-query constructions with polynomial space. Rosenthal subsequently gave uniform polynomial-size state preparation with one Boolean query when workspace may be discarded, and four when it must be cleared.

Why does this not immediately solve unitary synthesis? Preparing a column U∣j⟩U|j\rangleU∣j⟩ while retaining its input label gives ∣j⟩U∣j⟩|j\rangle U|j\rangle∣j⟩U∣j⟩. On a superposition of labels, discarding the first register can destroy coherence. Erasing that label while retaining the correct quantum output is a separate task.

For unitaries, Rosenthal obtained an upper bound of order 2n/22^{n/2}2n/2, up to polynomial factors, with a target-dependent oracle. Lombardi, Ma and Wright established a general one-query obstruction, also ruling out polynomially many parallel queries of polynomial length. Dong, Lombardi and Ma gave explicit one-query separations for structured unitary families. These bounds leave room for multiple queries interleaved with computation.

The manuscript also compares with the September 2026 Nehoran–Yuen construction, in the cited version. It achieves a constant number of suitable phase or Boolean queries but uses resources exponential in the number of input qubits. Thus the remaining issue is polynomial total resources, including the oracle interface width. The present claim addresses that requirement, not merely the number of queries.

4. What the new manuscript claims

There is a fixed polynomial ppp and a deterministic generator that, on input 1n1^n1n, outputs an oracle circuit AnA_nAn​ within time p(n)p(n)p(n). The circuit uses only

H,T=diag⁡(1,eiπ/4),T†,CNOT⁡H,\quad T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4}),\quad T^\dagger,\quad\operatorname{CNOT}H,T=diag(1,eiπ/4),T†,CNOT

and one Boolean oracle with input length m(n)≤p(n)m(n)\leq p(n)m(n)≤p(n). Its qubit count, elementary-gate count and oracle-call count are each at most p(n)p(n)p(n).

For every U∈U(2n)U\in U(2^n)U∈U(2n), there exists a Boolean function fff on those addresses such that

∥Φn,f−U∥⋄≤12.\|\Phi_{n,f}-\mathcal U\|_\diamond\leq\frac12.∥Φn,f​−U∥⋄​≤21​.

The quantifier order is essential:

one circuit Anfor every Uwith a suitable fU.\text{one circuit }A_n\quad\text{for every }U\quad\text{with a suitable }f_U.one circuit An​for every Uwith a suitable fU​.

There is no restriction on the truth-table size or classical circuit complexity of fUf_UfU​, and no prescribed matrix-entry encoding that the algorithm must use. The statement supplies an existence theorem for an encoding suited to the synthesis procedure.

Consequently this is not a polynomial-time classical compiler from an arbitrary explicitly listed unitary. It is also not an oracle-free polynomial-size implementation of every unitary. The target-dependent information remains in the oracle, whose evaluation is treated as a primitive query.

The headline guarantee is constant error in the full diamond norm. The proof obtains room within that bound through stronger intermediate estimates, but the reported theorem should not be replaced by an unstated optimal precision-resource tradeoff.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5, provisional. The result addresses a longstanding general synthesis problem and removes the exponential total-resource cost of earlier approaches in the stated oracle setting.

It clarifies how classical information can control a coherent quantum operation. State preparation alone leaves an input-label problem; the construction claims a way to erase that label efficiently while maintaining a uniform action on all inputs and references.

The distinction between storing and producing the oracle is central to its significance. The theorem says that an appropriate description can be used efficiently, not that every target admits a short efficiently computable classical description. This is a major structural result in oracle computation if correct, without implying a generic practical shortcut for compiling arbitrary quantum matrices.

6. The main idea

Reduce the dimension without duplicating the recursive call

The construction reduces synthesis of a ddd-dimensional unitary to synthesis of one smaller controlled unitary. Each step removes at least an inverse-polynomial fraction of the dimension. Since d≤2nd\leq2^nd≤2n, polynomially many steps suffice.

A recursive reduction can still become exponential if it calls the smaller synthesis routine several times at each level. The manuscript’s reduction uses that smaller routine exactly once, surrounded by two encoding operations. This is the key resource-accounting feature.

After suitable permutations, signs and Walsh transforms, partition the current unitary as

V=(ABCD),∥D∥≤34.V=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix},\qquad\|D\|\leq\frac34.V=(AC​BD​),∥D∥≤43​.

The lower block is the part to be removed. For a diagonal unitary ZZZ on those coordinates, feeding the lower output back into the lower input gives the transfer matrix

F=A+BZ(I−DZ)−1C.F=A+BZ(I-DZ)^{-1}C.F=A+BZ(I−DZ)−1C.

Because DDD is a contraction, the inverse has a convergent geometric-series expansion. Unitarity of VVV makes FFF unitary on the remaining coordinates.

Encode the feedback coherently

The manuscript builds forward and backward encoding maps from the original space into a phase-label register and a smaller state. Truncating the two geometric series gives nearly isometric maps and an approximate intertwining relation around one controlled application of FFF.

Averaging a common phase cancels terms of unequal degree. The remaining Gram-matrix sums telescope by unitarity, leaving errors that decay exponentially in truncation length. Thus the feedback identity becomes a controlled circuit reduction rather than merely a matrix formula.

Erase the input label through sparse rows

The encoders’ Fourier coefficients are arranged using frequencies (1,i,i2,…,iL)(1,i,i^2,\ldots,i^L)(1,i,i2,…,iL) for each removed coordinate iii. Products of at most LLL phases record coordinate multisets through power sums.

This arrangement means each row of the coefficient matrix has only polynomially many possible input labels, even when a column is dense. After coherently preparing a column, the circuit can use the short row list to erase the original input index. Amplitude amplification converts the resulting scaled map into the needed approximate encoding.

Finally, the proof begins with programmable controlled one-qubit gates and compiles their tables into finite words over the fixed gate set, read through a single Boolean oracle. The compilation preserves relative phases between different control labels. Uniform approximation on zero-workspace inputs, including reference systems, yields the final channel bound after workspace is discarded.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The oracle may be arbitrarily hard to construct or evaluate classically. Its assumed unit-cost availability is part of the model. There is no contradiction with counting arguments showing that most unitaries lack small ordinary circuits: the oracle carries a potentially enormous description.

The theorem allows polynomially many interleaved queries. It does not evade the earlier one-query or parallel-query lower bounds by claiming those restricted models suffice. It also counts query width, which distinguishes it from constant-query constructions with exponential workspace.

The stated target is constant-error channel synthesis. Efficient construction of useful oracles from natural descriptions, sharper precision dependence and practical gate counts are further questions. They are not supplied by the existence theorem itself.

8. Sources and further reading

Aaronson–Kuperberg’s original problem and the cited constant-query predecessor are linked above. Rosenthal’s query and depth upper bounds give the earlier exponential-time comparison. The source below provides the dimension-reduction, encoding and compilation claims, reported with their oracle quantifiers intact.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle (October 5, 2026).

Sources consulted on 25 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: When geometry and operator indices part company: three group-algebra counterexamples
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 285 · Operator algebras
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-25

1. The question

A group can be studied geometrically, through spaces on which it acts, or analytically, through operators that translate functions on the group. The Baum–Connes conjecture proposes a precise agreement between invariants obtained by these two routes. Geometric index classes should account for every analytic class, and distinct geometric classes should remain distinguishable analytically.

Family 285 contains three claimed counterexamples. One loses a nonzero geometric class. Another constructs an unexpected projection for a group without finite-order elements. The third constructs a projection whose irrational trace prevents it from coming from geometry. All concern the reduced, coefficient-free formulation. These adjectives distinguish the claims from earlier counterexamples to related formulations and from several conjectures that the manuscripts do not disprove.

2. Background and essential definitions

A discrete group GGG acts on the Hilbert space ℓ2(G)\ell^2(G)ℓ2(G) of square-summable functions by translation:

(λ(g)ξ)(h)=ξ(g−1h).(\lambda(g)\xi)(h)=\xi(g^{-1}h).(λ(g)ξ)(h)=ξ(g−1h).

Finite complex linear combinations of these operators form the represented group ring C[G]\mathbb C[G]C[G]. Closing it in operator norm gives the reduced group C-algebra* Cr∗(G)C_r^*(G)Cr∗​(G). A C*-algebra is an algebra of bounded operators closed under adjoints and norm limits. Norm completion allows operators that no finite group-ring expression describes.

A projection satisfies p=p∗=p2p=p^*=p^2p=p∗=p2; geometrically it projects onto a closed subspace. The canonical trace is

τG(a)=⟨aδe,δe⟩,\tau_G(a)=\langle a\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle,τG​(a)=⟨aδe​,δe​⟩,

where eee is the identity and δe\delta_eδe​ its unit point mass. Thus τG(1)=1\tau_G(1)=1τG​(1)=1. On a matrix algebra the trace is the unnormalized sum of diagonal traces, not their average.

The group K0(A)K_0(A)K0​(A) records stable differences of projections over a C*-algebra AAA; stabilization permits matrices of arbitrary finite size. Accordingly, a matrix projection and a projection in AAA itself are different objects. The latter is sometimes called a scalar projection, meaning a one-by-one matrix over the algebra, not necessarily a scalar multiple of the identity.

For a torsion-free group, whose only finite-order element is its identity, assembly takes the form

μr:K∗(BG)⟶K∗(Cr∗(G)).\mu_r:K_*(BG)\longrightarrow K_*(C_r^*(G)).μr​:K∗​(BG)⟶K∗​(Cr∗​(G)).

Here BGBGBG is a classifying space for the group and the left side is topological K-homology, built from geometric index data with compact support. For groups with torsion one instead uses equivariant K-homology of the classifying space for proper actions, where stabilizers are finite. The conjecture asserts that assembly is an isomorphism.

“Coefficient-free” means coefficients C\mathbb CC with trivial action. Allowing a separate algebra carrying a group action gives a stronger conjecture. “Reduced” specifies the regular representation above; the maximal group C*-algebra uses all unitary representations and need not give the same K-theory.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Baum and Connes developed the index-theoretic comparison beginning with a manuscript circulated in 1982. The formulation with Higson made proper actions and general coefficient algebras central to its scope. Positive results cover large classes: Higson–Kasparov’s theorem applies to groups admitting proper affine isometric actions on Hilbert space, while work of Mineyev–Yu and Lafforgue establishes major hyperbolic-group cases.

Higson, Lafforgue and Skandalis constructed influential counterexamples using expander geometry. Their discrete-group counterexamples concern nontrivial coefficients; their groupoid examples concern a different kind of symmetry object. Neither is already the coefficient-free group counterexample claimed here. Exact crossed-product reformulations were subsequently developed to respond to those failures, and are again separate assertions.

The projection question has a parallel history. Kadison and Kaplansky’s conjecture predicts that a torsion-free group’s reduced algebra has no projections other than zero and one. Pimsner–Voiculescu established the free-group case. More generally, for torsion-free groups the canonical trace is integral on the assembly image, so surjectivity of assembly forces scalar projectionlessness.

Other constructions, including Austin’s, produced irrational dimensions of kernels of group-ring operators. These live naturally in a larger group von Neumann algebra, closed in a weaker operator topology. Their kernel projections need not belong to the reduced C*-algebra. That membership issue is decisive: some groups with irrational von Neumann kernel dimensions already satisfy Baum–Connes.

The new manuscripts therefore seek more than unusual kernel dimensions or another coefficient obstruction. They require precise failures inside the coefficient-free reduced-algebra setting.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

M1: a geometric class that disappears

M1 constructs a finitely generated torsion-free group GinjG_{\mathrm{inj}}Ginj​, an embedding i:Z2→Ginji:\mathbb Z^2\to G_{\mathrm{inj}}i:Z2→Ginj​, and an integral degree-two cohomology class detecting the embedded torus. The torus’s Dirac K-homology class gives an infinite-order element hhh with

h⊗1≠0,μr(h)=0.h\otimes1\ne0,\qquad \mu_r(h)=0.h⊗1=0,μr​(h)=0.

The tensor product with Q\mathbb QQ in the first expression means that the class survives after ignoring torsion. Thus M1 claims failure even of rational injectivity. Analytically, the rank-zero Bott class associated with the torus becomes zero; geometrically, the integral cohomology pairing keeps the original class nonzero. Finite presentation is not claimed.

M2: a forbidden projection without torsion

M2 constructs a finitely generated torsion-free group GprojG_{\mathrm{proj}}Gproj​ and a projection in its reduced algebra satisfying

0<τGproj(e)<12.0<\tau_{G_{\mathrm{proj}}}(e)<\frac12.0<τGproj​​(e)<21​.

It is therefore neither zero nor the identity, contradicting the projection form of Kadison–Kaplansky. The nonintegral trace also obstructs coefficient-free reduced assembly surjectivity. This is an actual projection in the algebra itself, after a separate step converting a small-trace matrix projection into a scalar one.

M2 cites a companion result that the same group’s complex group ring still has no nontrivial scalar idempotents. The claimed failure occurs in the norm completion; it is not a counterexample to that algebraic group-ring assertion.

M3: an irrational analytic class

M3 constructs a finitely generated discrete group GsurG_{\mathrm{sur}}Gsur​ and a scalar projection b0∈Cr∗(Gsur)b_0\in C_r^*(G_{\mathrm{sur}})b0​∈Cr∗​(Gsur​) with irrational canonical trace. Lück’s trace theorem makes every degree-zero assembly image rational, so

[b0]∉im⁡μr.[b_0]\notin\operatorname{im}\mu_r.[b0​]∈/imμr​.

This group is built using a module over a finite field and is not asserted torsion-free. The three manuscripts construct separate groups; the family does not identify one example simultaneously having every listed property.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5. If correct, these constructions overturn central predictions linking group geometry, index theory and operator algebras. They claim both kinds of assembly failure: geometric information can disappear, and analytic information can exist without a geometric preimage.

The projection example is particularly concrete. It says that a torsion-free group can acquire a nontrivial orthogonal decomposition inside its completed translation algebra despite the absence of finite-order group elements. The irrational-trace example supplies a numerical obstruction that can be described without calculating the entire K-theory group.

The distinctions also limit the conclusion. A failure of the reduced comparison does not erase the successful theorems for amenable, hyperbolic or other covered groups. Nor does it automatically contradict the maximal assembly formulation or the classical Novikov conjecture about higher signatures of manifolds.

6. The main idea

Create controlled geometry at many scales

All three constructions use graph geometry to manufacture analytic phenomena while controlling the ambient group. Expanders are finite graphs with strong connectivity, reflected in a uniform spectral gap separating constant functions from oscillating ones. Carefully chosen labels let large graph pieces embed in a group’s Cayley graph, the graph describing multiplication by generators.

A major construction issue is simultaneous overlap: controlling one pair of graph copies is insufficient when infinitely many translated copies interact. The manuscripts organize copies so that overlaps and unused edges can be estimated together. The detailed constructions differ between papers; expander terminology alone is not a substitute for those estimates.

Cancel a Bott class while preserving its detector

M1 places localized Bott representatives at successive heights. One homotopy identifies even-height and odd-height families; a second identifies odd heights with positive even heights. Together they identify a family with the same family minus its initial term, forcing that term’s K-class to vanish.

This resembles cancellation in an infinite sequence, but the representatives must be bounded operators and the homotopies must genuinely belong to the relevant norm-algebra construction. A separate geometric ingredient preserves an embedded torus and extends its integral cohomology detector. The analytic cancellation and topological survival are deliberately built together, then retained in a finitely generated subgroup.

Use a spectral gap to obtain an actual projection

M2 constructs a finite matrix group-ring operator with a separated spectral band and very small positive projection trace. A gap makes the band indicator continuous on the spectrum, so continuous functional calculus places its projection in the reduced C*-algebra. Adjoining finitely many free generators then permits compression to a scalar projection of the same trace, while preserving torsion-freeness and finite generation.

M3 uses local finite-field rules to select isolated expander components. Its operator has a kernel consisting of constants on selected components, with a uniform gap on the entire remainder. The trace becomes a series of powers p−kip^{-k_i}p−ki​, where ppp is a prime and the chosen exponents make the base-ppp expansion nonperiodic. That yields irrationality. The global gap, rather than the trace calculation alone, puts the kernel projection in the reduced algebra.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

These are existence constructions with finite generation, not claims of practical small presentations or useful numerical parameter bounds. M1 explicitly does not assert finite presentation. The group constructions and spectral realizations are part of the manuscripts’ mathematical claims, reported here without proof verification.

For M1, established low-degree nonvanishing results still detect its class under maximal assembly. The class is lost on passing to the reduced completion. Consequently the claimed reduced rational-injectivity failure does not disprove maximal rational injectivity or classical Novikov. Terminology such as “strong Novikov” varies, so specifying the completion is essential.

Likewise, projections in a von Neumann algebra, matrices over a reduced C*-algebra, the reduced algebra itself, and the algebraic group ring have different implications. The papers carefully move between these settings only when an additional construction permits it.
