This is different from probability-one behavior. The argument removes auxiliary parameters using category, without assigning a probability distribution to them.

A Borel function has inverse images of open sets belonging to the sigma-algebra generated by open sets. Such functions have enough regularity to become continuous after restriction to a suitable comeager subset. This does not mean they are continuous at every point of the original space.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Turing introduced oracle computation in his 1939 work on systems of logic based on ordinals. The degree structure subsequently became a central object of computability theory: it organizes what can be computed relative to what, without retaining a preferred presentation of each oracle.

The automorphism problem gradually became more constrained. Jockusch and Solovay showed that every jump-preserving order automorphism fixes all degrees above 0(4)\mathbf0^{(4)}0(4). Shore and Slaman later proved that the jump is definable from the degree ordering, using Slaman–Woodin’s definability of the double jump. Consequently, jump preservation is automatic for order automorphisms.

Nerode and Shore proved that every automorphism fixes some cone, though the cone could depend on the automorphism. Slaman and Woodin obtained a common fixed cone: every automorphism fixes every degree above 0′′\mathbf0''0′′. They also showed that the automorphism group is countable and developed arithmetic representations of its elements.

These results leave a sharp remaining question. Fixing all sufficiently high degrees does not by itself force every lower degree to be fixed. A nontrivial automorphism might act only outside the known fixed cone while preserving all comparisons with it.

The new paper uses an external theorem from Slaman and Woodin’s unpublished 2005 manuscript Definability in Degree Structures, also presented in Slaman’s later account. In the all-input form cited by the paper, every arbitrary degree automorphism has one arithmetic function on sets of integers that induces it at every input. The all-input scope is important; a representation only on generic inputs would be a different premise.

There are also methodological predecessors involving recovery of real parameters. Groszek–Slaman and Lutz–Siskind recover reals from finitely many branches of perfect sets under appropriate hypotheses. Kjos-Hanssen proved rigidity for automorphisms induced by permutations of the natural numbers, using parameter recovery and a measure cone theorem. The present manuscript claims a different recovery mechanism based on addition and Baire category, applicable to representatives of arbitrary degree automorphisms.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

The main theorem is

Aut⁡(DT,≤T)={id}. \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D_T,\leq_T)=\{\mathrm{id}\}.Aut(DT​,≤T​)={id}.

No effective presentation, continuity, Borelness or arithmetic definition is required of π\piπ in this statement. The cited representation theorem supplies regularity on the level of chosen oracle representatives.

The manuscript also gives a recovery theorem that is stated independently of automorphisms. Encode a real number xxx by its strict rational cut C(x)C(x)C(x), the set of indices of rational numbers below xxx. Suppose

F:R⟶2N F:\mathbb R\longrightarrow2^{\mathbb N}F:R⟶2N

is Borel, has countable fibers, and satisfies

F(x+y)≤TF(x)⊕F(y)for all x,y∈R. F(x+y)\leq_T F(x)\oplus F(y) \quad\text{for all }x,y\in\mathbb R.F(x+y)≤T​F(x)⊕F(y)for all x,y∈R.

Countable fibers means that each output has at most countably many real preimages. For any irrational t∈(0,1)t\in(0,1)t∈(0,1), the theorem claims that for a comeager set of pairs (u,v)(u,v)(u,v), some rational δ∈(0,1)\delta\in(0,1)δ∈(0,1) gives

C(t)≤TF(u)⊕F(u−v)⊕F(v−u+δt)⊕F(v−u+δ(t−1)).\begin{aligned} C(t)\leq_T {}&F(u)\oplus F(u-v)\\ &\oplus F(v-u+\delta t)\\ &\oplus F(v-u+\delta(t-1)).\end{aligned}C(t)≤T​​F(u)⊕F(u−v)⊕F(v−u+δt)⊕F(v−u+δ(t−1)).​

The four displayed values are the only real oracles used. Program indices and rational constants may depend on the particular parameters; the theorem does not claim an effective uniform selection of them.

Finally, the paper derives the Slaman–Woodin biinterpretability conjecture from their established equivalence with rigidity. In that precise formulation, the degree order and full second-order arithmetic can be interpreted in each other without parameters, including a definable relation matching a coded set of integers to its Turing degree.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5, provisional. Rigidity would settle a foundational question about whether the abstract order of relative computational power retains enough information to distinguish every degree.

The biinterpretability consequence strengthens the significance: through the cited equivalence, the result connects the apparently sparse language of one partial order with the much richer structure of natural numbers and all their subsets.

The recovery theorem is also a concrete proposed mechanism. It extracts one real parameter from four outputs of a function constrained only by Borel regularity, countable fibers and an addition reducibility relation.

This score does not mean that every degree has a short explicit definition, or that an algorithm can identify arbitrary degrees. Rigidity and effective classification are different notions. The definability consequence uses the specific Slaman–Woodin equivalence, not a general principle that every rigid structure has all elements individually definable.

6. The main idea

Represent the automorphism by a Borel function

For an arbitrary automorphism π\piπ, the cited theorem gives an arithmetic representative F^\widehat FF on subsets of N\mathbb NN, with output degree π([A]T)\pi([A]_T)π([A]T​) on every input AAA.

Compose with rational-cut coding to obtain F(x)=F^(C(x))F(x)=\widehat F(C(x))F(x)=F(C(x)). This is Borel. Each fiber is countable because all its inputs have the same Turing degree, and a fixed oracle can compute only countably many sets through the countably many programs.

Real addition is computable at the level of degree bounds. Since π\piπ preserves joins, the resulting FFF satisfies the addition inequality required by the recovery theorem.

Encode the parameter in a bounded walk

Start with a real state s0=0s_0=0s0​=0. At each stage choose one of two increments,

δtorδ(t−1), \delta t\quad\text{or}\quad\delta(t-1),δtorδ(t−1),

recording the choice by rn=0r_n=0rn​=0 or rn=1r_n=1rn​=1, respectively. After NNN steps,

sN=δ(Nt−∑n<Nrn). s_N=\delta\left(Nt-\sum_{n<N}r_n\right).sN​=δ(Nt−n<N∑​rn​).

If the states remain bounded in absolute value by one, then

∣t−1N∑n<Nrn∣<1Nδ. \left|t-\frac1N\sum_{n<N}r_n\right|<\frac1{N\delta}.​t−N1​n<N∑​rn​​<Nδ1​.

The average of the binary choices therefore recovers ttt with an effective error bound. Because ttt is irrational, sufficiently accurate approximations eventually answer every rational-cut query.

The challenge is to compute the choices without having ttt as an oracle. Countable fibers and continuity on a comeager restriction supply an output bit that takes different values near two positions. Testing that bit of F(u+sn)F(u+s_n)F(u+sn​) forces the walk inward near the two endpoints. Its behavior in the middle need not be monotone.

Four fixed values update the walk

Borel regularity also supplies two addition programs that remain fixed along the selected recurrence. One moves from the neighborhood of uuu to that of vvv, adding the chosen increment; the other returns to the neighborhood of uuu.

The initial value, return value and two possible increment values are exactly the four oracles in the theorem. Recursive substitution of these programs computes the next tested bit from the previous ones.

The algorithm computes the choices rnr_nrn​, not the numerical states sns_nsn​. This avoids silently supplying the unknown real parameter as extra information. There is no asserted running-time bound; each requested bit is obtained after a finite computation.

Remove the auxiliary reals

Let d(x)d(x)d(x) be the degree of C(x)C(x)C(x). The four arguments are rational affine combinations of t,u,vt,u,vt,u,v, so recovery implies, after applying the inverse automorphism,

π−1(d(t))≤Td(t)∨d(u)∨d(v) \pi^{-1}(d(t))\leq_Td(t)\vee d(u)\vee d(v)π−1(d(t))≤T​d(t)∨d(u)∨d(v)

for a comeager set of pairs.

A relative category cone-avoidance theorem says that if a fixed set is not computable from a fixed oracle, the pairs of auxiliary reals that make it computable form only a meager set. Thus the displayed comeager recovery forces

π−1(d(t))≤Td(t). \pi^{-1}(d(t))\leq_Td(t).π−1(d(t))≤T​d(t).

Every noncomputable degree has an irrational representative of this kind, and the computable degree is automatically fixed. Applying the same argument to π−1\pi^{-1}π−1, and using order preservation, gives both inequalities between π(a)\pi(\mathbf a)π(a) and a\mathbf aa. Antisymmetry yields equality.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The claim covers arbitrary automorphisms of the full degree order. The proof’s regularity comes from the all-input representation theorem, which is an essential external dependency and is explicitly attributed to the 2005 Slaman–Woodin manuscript.

The representing Borel function need not be injective and need not have a functional inverse. The final symmetry argument represents the inverse degree automorphism separately.

Comeager recovery is topological, not a probability-one statement. The reductions may vary with the auxiliary pair, which the category-avoidance argument allows by ranging over all program indices.

The theorem does not give an efficient procedure for comparing arbitrary Turing degrees or computing the recovered parameter without its four oracles. Questions about automorphisms of other reducibility structures or restricted degree substructures are not automatically settled by full Turing-degree rigidity.

8. Sources and further reading

Turing, Systems of logic based on ordinals, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 45 (1939), 161–228, introduces oracle computation. Shore and Slaman, Defining the Turing jump, Mathematical Research Letters 6 (1999), 711–722, gives the jump-definability theorem.

Slaman and Woodin, Definability in Degree Structures, unpublished manuscript dated 21 July 2005, is the source cited for the all-input representation and rigidity–biinterpretability equivalence. Slaman, Global properties of the Turing degrees and the Turing jump, in Computational Prospects of Infinity, Part I (2008), 83–101, presents related results.

Kjos-Hanssen, Permutations of the integers induce only the trivial automorphism of the Turing degrees, Bulletin of Symbolic Logic 24 (2018), 165–174, is the parameter-recovery predecessor. Lutz and Siskind, Part 1 of Martin’s conjecture for order-preserving and measure-preserving functions, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 38 (2025), 319–367, supplies a related finite-oracle perfect-set recovery theorem.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Rigidity of the Turing degrees (September 24, 2026).

Sources consulted on 21 October 2026 at repository revision 1581d4c. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Encoding every accepting computation by exactly one Diophantine witness
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 242 · Mathematical logic
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-21

1. The question

A polynomial equation with integer coefficients can encode a computer program. Given an input, the equation can have a natural-number solution exactly when the program eventually accepts that input. This is the arithmetic universality behind the negative solution of Hilbert’s tenth problem.

But the encoding usually permits many solutions for one accepting computation. Extra variables may describe the same rational number in different ways, choose different arithmetic certificates, or use different bases to store the run.

Can all that redundancy be removed? Family 242 contains a manuscript dated 24 September 2026 claiming that every computably enumerable relation has a polynomial representation with exactly one complete auxiliary tuple for each member. This is the single-fold conjecture, and it implies the weaker finite-fold conjecture.

2. Background and essential definitions

Enumerable does not mean decidable

Throughout, N={0,1,2,…}\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}N={0,1,2,…}. A set S⊆NnS\subseteq\mathbb N^nS⊆Nn is computably enumerable, also called recursively enumerable, if a deterministic machine accepts exactly its members. On a nonmember, the machine may run forever.

A decidable set has an algorithm that halts on every input and answers both yes and no correctly. The halting problem is a standard example of a computably enumerable set that is not decidable.

A Diophantine representation of SSS is a polynomial with integer coefficients,

P(A1,…,An,W1,…,Wm), P(A_1,\ldots,A_n,W_1,\ldots,W_m),P(A1​,…,An​,W1​,…,Wm​),

such that an input aaa belongs to SSS precisely when some auxiliary tuple w∈Nmw\in\mathbb N^mw∈Nm satisfies P(a,w)=0P(a,w)=0P(a,w)=0. The input variables are fixed; only the witness variables are searched over.

Counting the whole witness

The representation is single-fold if there is exactly one witness tuple for every member and none for every nonmember. It is finite-fold if each input has only finitely many witnesses.

“Complete tuple” includes every variable introduced inside the construction. A unique accepting run is not enough if a subsidiary equation allows several quotient choices, rational-coordinate encodings or inactive branch variables.

For example, the inequality u≥vu\geq vu≥v can be encoded by u−v=su-v=su−v=s with s∈Ns\in\mathbb Ns∈N. Once u,vu,vu,v are fixed, this slack variable is unique. Division by a positive integer can be encoded by

a=dq+r,0≤r<d, a=dq+r,\qquad 0\leq r<d,a=dq+r,0≤r<d,

which fixes both quotient and remainder. By contrast, an unrestricted equation expressing coprimality through Bézout coefficients usually has many solutions, so it requires normalization.

A finite list of polynomial equations can be replaced over N\mathbb NN by one equation:

F12+⋯+Fs2=0. F_1^2+\cdots+F_s^2=0.F12​+⋯+Fs2​=0.

This introduces no new variables and preserves the entire solution set. The difficult issue is therefore unique polynomial systems, not the final conversion from a system to one polynomial.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Julia Robinson developed a route from sufficiently strong Diophantine growth conditions to exponentiation. Davis, Putnam and Robinson proved that every recursively enumerable relation has an exponential Diophantine representation, permitting exponentiation in addition to ordinary polynomial operations.

Matiyasevich’s 1970 construction supplied the growth needed to replace exponentiation and complete the polynomial representation theorem. Together these results solved Hilbert’s tenth problem negatively: an algorithm deciding polynomial solvability would decide every computably enumerable set, including undecidable ones.

That theorem does not control the number of witnesses. In 1974, Matiyasevich proved a stronger uniqueness theorem for exponential representations: every recursively enumerable relation has an exponential representation with one complete auxiliary tuple. The same work identified single-fold binary exponentiation as the crucial remaining polynomial problem.

The single-fold and finite-fold conjectures ask whether uniqueness, or at least finiteness, survives after exponentiation has been eliminated. This is not merely a reformulation of the original representation theorem. Replacing a concise operation by an existential polynomial construction can introduce many internal witnesses.

There are important positive results in other domains. Miller and Shlapentokh obtained single-fold definitions using witnesses in characteristic-zero polynomial rings, and finite-fold definitions over related rings of functions. Those results do not give the natural-number witness theorem claimed here.

The new manuscript combines classical Pell-equation methods with rank-one elliptic-curve heights. Poonen’s use of elliptic curves and denominator growth in Diophantine definability is a predecessor, while Jones and Matiyasevich’s register-machine and bit-masking methods supply the computational encoding framework. The advertised new arithmetic step is a uniquely represented growth function strong enough to select exact Pell indices.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

For every n≥1n\geq1n≥1 and every computably enumerable S⊆NnS\subseteq\mathbb N^nS⊆Nn, the manuscript asserts the existence of m≥1m\geq1m≥1 and an integer polynomial PPP such that

#{w∈Nm:P(a,w)=0}={1,a∈S,0,a∉S. \#\{w\in\mathbb N^m:P(a,w)=0\} =\begin{cases} 1,&a\in S,\\ 0,&a\notin S. \end{cases}#{w∈Nm:P(a,w)=0}={1,0,​a∈S,a∈/S.​

All auxiliary variables, including those implementing arithmetic subroutines, count toward this uniqueness. The variables range over nonnegative integers, not arbitrary rational numbers, integer tuples with unrestricted signs, or a polynomial-ring witness domain.

The main undecidability consequence has a strong promise. There exist fixed integers m,D≥1m,D\geq1m,D≥1 such that no algorithm can, for every polynomial in mmm variables of degree at most DDD known to have at most one natural-number solution, always halt and decide whether a solution exists.

The input is promised to have zero or one solution. The algorithm is not being asked to verify the promise. Nor is this the trivial promise of exactly one solution, under which the answer would already be yes.

The construction uses arithmetic constants fixed independently of the enumerable set and its inputs. The paper establishes their existence but does not supply all their numerical values, the final expanded polynomial coefficients, or a procedure for numerically choosing those constants. Its theorem is an existence result for the polynomial, rather than a displayed practical compiler.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5, provisional. The theorem would settle longstanding refinements of the Diophantine representation theorem and show that undecidability persists even when each equation has at most one witness.

This separates difficulty caused by searching a large or redundant solution space from difficulty intrinsic to existence. Removing all multiplicity would still leave an undecidable solvability problem.

Uniqueness also strengthens the correspondence between computation and arithmetic. Every accepting input would determine one arithmetic certificate, with no alternative encodings hidden in the auxiliary variables.

The score concerns that theoretical strengthening. It does not provide an efficient way to find the unique solution, a computable bound on its size, or a decision procedure for the promised class. Indeed, the claimed undecidability consequence rules out the last possibility.

6. The main idea

Normalize every arithmetic choice

The construction begins with a discipline for polynomial encodings. Integers use a unique positive–negative sign code. Rational numbers use reduced numerator–denominator data together with normalized inverse witnesses. Quotients, remainders and inequality slacks are fixed by their arguments.

Case distinctions require special care. A selector chooses one active branch, and every local variable in each inactive branch is forced to zero. Otherwise a branch that contributes no equation could still introduce arbitrarily many witnesses.

These conventions are carried through composition. A subsidiary call contributes its full internal tuple, so uniqueness cannot be lost silently inside an arithmetic abbreviation.

Obtain a uniquely represented growth function

The arithmetic construction uses the elliptic curve

E:y2=x3−25x. E:\quad y^2=x^3-25x.E:y2=x3−25x.

The manuscript supplies a rank-one calculation: its rational points have the form nP+tnP+tnP+t, where n∈Zn\in\mathbb Zn∈Z, PPP is a fixed generator of the free part and ttt belongs to a finite torsion subgroup.

A normalized representative is selected for each positive absolute index. After a fixed scalar multiplication, let WjW_jWj​ be the maximum of the absolute numerator and positive denominator of the reduced x-coordinate. Height theory gives

log⁡Wj=aEj2+O(1),aE>0, \log W_j=a_Ej^2+O(1),\qquad a_E>0,logWj​=aE​j2+O(1),aE​>0,

with a uniformly bounded error. The chosen scalar enlarges the quadratic coefficient enough to separate the integer indices while retaining a controlled error.

The useful comparison is a discrete difference:

log⁡W2kWrW1Wk2Wr+1=2aE(k2−r)+O(1). \log\frac{W_{2k}W_rW_1}{W_k^2W_{r+1}} =2a_E(k^2-r)+O(1).logWk2​Wr+1​W2k​Wr​W1​​=2aE​(k2−r)+O(1).

A fixed multiplicative window around the ratio therefore singles out r=k2r=k^2r=k2. The polynomial system uses point additions, products and comparisons; the indices and logarithms appear in the explanatory growth argument, not as extra polynomial operations.

For an input uuu, bracket it uniquely between consecutive heights and output the height at the squared index. The resulting function g(u)g(u)g(u) has a single-fold polynomial graph and intermediate growth, with bounds of the form

δ(log⁡u)2<log⁡g(u)<ulog⁡u \delta(\log u)^2<\log g(u)<u\log uδ(logu)2<logg(u)<ulogu

for sufficiently large uuu and a fixed δ>0\delta>0δ>0.

Use growth to pin down powers

Pell equations have recursively ordered families of solutions with rapidly growing coordinates. Congruences can constrain the solution index, but a congruence alone usually identifies only a residue class of indices.

The new growth function supplies a cutoff. Its upper bound forces the relevant indices below a modulus, turning congruence information into exact equality. Its lower bound ensures that the intended solutions are still admitted.

An integer quotient then recovers c=bnc=b^nc=bn, with a unique complete witness for every b≥2b\geq2b≥2 and n≥0n\geq0n≥0. This is the single-fold power graph needed to eliminate exponentiation from the computational encoding.

Pack one deterministic run into integers

A deterministic counter machine has a unique run on each input. The manuscript stores its successive states and counter values as digits of finitely many integers in a large base.

Binary-containment tests, implemented through powers and Lucas’s binomial parity criterion, restrict which digits can be nonzero. Polynomial identities enforce legal transitions and the first accepting halt.

A clock and a dyadic interval select one power-of-two base for the entire run. This prevents the same history from being encoded in many larger bases. Once the run and base are fixed, every displayed integer and every internal arithmetic witness is fixed.

The number of variables depends on the chosen machine and fixed arithmetic constructions, not on the particular input or its halting time. Very long computations are stored in very large integers rather than by introducing a new variable for every step.

Derive the promise result

Apply the representation theorem to one fixed undecidable computably enumerable set. Substituting an input tuple into the parameter variables produces a polynomial in the same fixed number of witness variables, with a fixed degree bound.

Every resulting polynomial has at most one solution. A solver for the promised class would decide membership in the original undecidable set. This establishes the claimed impossibility without requiring a uniform algorithm that constructs representations for all enumerable sets.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The theorem counts solutions over N\mathbb NN, including zero. Passing to other witness domains requires separate uniqueness-preserving translations; it should not be assumed from the statement alone.

The claimed polynomial and the promise parameters m,Dm,Dm,D exist, but the manuscript does not provide a small explicit universal equation or numerical values for every fixed constant. The result is therefore distinct from optimizing the degree, number of variables or coefficient sizes.

Single-fold representation gives no computable stopping rule for searching a negative instance. On positive instances, exhaustive enumeration eventually finds the unique witness; on negative instances it can continue forever.

A unique witness may also be extraordinarily large. Bounds on solution size would have additional algorithmic consequences, and no general computable bound is claimed here. The finite-fold conclusion follows immediately from uniqueness, but its broader quantitative refinements are separate questions.

8. Sources and further reading

Davis, Putnam and Robinson, The decision problem for exponential Diophantine equations, Annals of Mathematics 74 (1961), 425–436, is the exponential representation theorem. Matiyasevich, The Diophantineness of enumerable sets (1970), completes the polynomial representation route.

Matiyasevich, The existence of non-effectivizable estimates in the theory of exponential Diophantine equations, Zapiski Nauchnykh Seminarov LOMI 40 (1974), 77–93, gives the single-fold exponential theorem. His Towards finite-fold Diophantine representations, Zapiski Nauchnykh Seminarov POMI 377 (2010), 78–90, discusses the finite-fold program.

Jones and Matiyasevich, Register machine proof of the theorem on exponential Diophantine representation of enumerable sets, Journal of Symbolic Logic 49 (1984), 818–829, supplies the computational predecessor. Poonen, Using elliptic curves of rank one towards the undecidability of Hilbert’s tenth problem over rings of algebraic integers, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 2369 (2002), 33–42, provides the elliptic-curve context. Cantone, Cuzziol and Omodeo, On Diophantine singlefold specifications, Le Matematiche 79 (2024), 585–620, discusses the Pell and uniqueness machinery.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Single-fold Diophantine representations (September 24, 2026).
