At singularities, taking the dual of the module of differentials and then taking a fiber need not reproduce the dual of the fiber of differentials. Thus one cannot dismiss the conjecture by saying that a free rank-two derivation module automatically makes the pointwise tangent space two-dimensional. That implication is part of the subtlety being investigated.

Normality and resolutions

An integral ring is normal if it is integrally closed in its fraction field. Geometrically, normality rules out some elementary defects, such as branches that should have been separated, but it still permits isolated singularities on surfaces.

A resolution replaces a singular point by a configuration of smooth curves in a smooth surface. These exceptional curves record information hidden at the point. Their genera, intersections, and the behavior of differential forms along them help determine the severity of the singularity.

The manuscript builds the neighborhood of one such curve first and then contracts the curve to produce the singular point.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Lipman’s 1965 work established that local freeness of the derivation module forces normality. The conjecture therefore asks whether free vector fields also rule out the normal singularities that remain.

In positive characteristic, the corresponding assertion can fail because differentiation loses information: for example, the derivative of zpz^pzp vanishes in characteristic ppp. Those examples do not settle the complex case, where ordinary differentiation behaves differently.

Strong positive results cover several broad classes in characteristic zero. Hochster treated positively graded algebras with degree-zero part equal to the field. Scheja–Storch handled hypersurfaces, and Källström’s corrected complete-intersection result handles the more general locally complete-intersection setting. Van Straten–Steenbrink proved the isolated-singularity case in dimension at least three using extension of differential forms, leaving surfaces as a distinct difficulty.

The extension viewpoint also connects the problem to birational singularities. Greb–Kebekus–Kovács–Peternell proved the conjecture for Kawamata log terminal spaces. Druel and Graf–Kovács established the log-canonical case, a larger class of mild singularities measured by discrepancies on resolutions.

For surfaces, Graf obtained results in low geometric genus. Bergner–Graf proved smoothness when

pg−g−b≤2,p_g-g-b\le2,pg​−g−b≤2,

where pgp_gpg​ is the geometric genus of the local singularity, ggg the sum of the genera of exceptional curves, and bbb the first Betti number of the resolution’s dual graph. Here the local geometric genus measures a cohomological obstruction on a resolution; it is not the geometric genus of a compact surface from the classification theory.

Another useful distinction is the Lie bracket. Jörder proved smoothness when a tangent basis can be chosen with pairwise commuting vector fields. Arbitrary free vector fields need not commute, whereas coordinate vector fields do.

M1 places its example outside these established classes. The neighborhood is deliberately not a positively graded cone, the singularity is more severe than log canonical, and no commuting tangent frame is claimed.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

Theorem 1.1 asserts a finitely generated normal integral complex algebra AAA of dimension two and a maximal ideal m\mathfrak mm such that

Der⁡C(A)≃A⊕2,Am is not regular.\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb C}(A)\simeq A^{\oplus2},\qquad A_{\mathfrak m}\text{ is not regular}.DerC​(A)≃A⊕2,Am​ is not regular.

The affine surface X=Spec⁡AX=\operatorname{Spec}AX=SpecA can be chosen smooth away from the marked singular point. The claim is therefore a counterexample with an isolated normal surface singularity and a globally free tangent sheaf.

The analytic precursor has one exceptional curve of genus 21 and self-intersection −10-10−10. M1 reports canonical discrepancy −5-5−5 and local geometric genus at least 33. Thus, for this resolution,

g=21,b=0,pg−g−b≥12.g=21,\qquad b=0,\qquad p_g-g-b\ge12.g=21,b=0,pg​−g−b≥12.

These values locate the proposed example beyond the earlier numerical smoothness criterion. The discrepancy is the coefficient measuring the change of the canonical divisor along the exceptional curve; log-canonical singularities require it to be at least −1-1−1.

Two further conclusions follow in the manuscript. First, the smooth locus U=XregU=X_{\mathrm{reg}}U=Xreg​ has logarithmic Kodaira dimension two, by applying an earlier theorem of Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte. Logarithmic Kodaira dimension measures the growth of canonical forms allowed logarithmic poles along a boundary compactifying UUU.

Second, repeatedly blowing up at the module of derivations does not resolve this singularity. The relevant blowup is designed to make the module locally free. Since it already is free, the operation is the identity; normalization also changes nothing because the surface is normal. This addresses the specific derivation-module procedure, not resolution of singularities by arbitrary blowups.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5. If correct, the construction would disprove a longstanding intrinsic criterion for smoothness in characteristic zero, in a dimension central to the remaining difficulty.

Vector fields are among the most basic local geometric objects. A free tangent sheaf looks formally like the tangent bundle of a smooth surface, so a counterexample would show that this module alone can miss singular geometry. The issue is not a shortage of vector fields but the failure of their algebraic organization to force coordinate directions.

The example would also clarify the reach of existing theorems. Their additional hypotheses—mild singularities, low resolution genus, grading, complete intersections, or commuting vector fields—carry essential information. The proposed counterexample does not negate those results; it would show why a general converse requires more than freeness.

6. The main idea

Start with a curve whose neighborhood can be changed

M1 chooses a smooth curve CCC of genus 21 and a degree-ten line bundle LLL satisfying

L⊗4≃KC.L^{\otimes4}\simeq K_C.L⊗4≃KC​.

The dual line bundle L−1L^{-1}L−1 has negative degree. Its zero section gives a starting neighborhood with normal bundle L−1L^{-1}L−1, but the manuscript modifies the holomorphic gluing of that neighborhood. This changes more than the normal bundle records.

In local base and fiber coordinates (z,t)(z,t)(z,t), the construction uses the meromorphic two-form

σ=t−5 dt∧dz.\sigma=t^{-5}\,dt\wedge dz.σ=t−5dt∧dz.

The aim is to build two vector fields whose determinant vanishes to exactly the required order along CCC, while remaining nonzero everywhere off CCC. They then form a tangent frame on the punctured neighborhood.

Match local corrections with global residue constraints

The leading coefficients of the fields have six common zeros on CCC. Correcting the determinant at those points requires local choices, but arbitrary choices need not glue around the whole curve.

An auxiliary elliptic curve and a trace pairing provide meromorphic data whose residues satisfy the needed global cancellation identities. The construction then extends the vector fields and their desired determinant through finitely many Taylor orders. Choosing determinant coefficients separately retains freedom to remove the compatibility obstructions.

The manuscript emphasizes a finite construction. It does not rely on asserting that an uncontrolled infinite sequence of neighborhood changes converges. Cohomological vanishing and formal-functions arguments are used to lift the finite data to actual holomorphic fields after shrinking the neighborhood.

Contract, then pass from analytic to algebraic geometry

Grauert’s contraction criterion collapses the negative curve to a point. The vector fields give a frame away from that point, and M1 uses normality to extend tangent freeness across it. Adjunction records that the resulting point is nonetheless singular.

The volume form dual to the frame has a fifth-order pole along the exceptional curve. The construction therefore does not assume the holomorphic extension of forms that powers many earlier positive results.

Finally, approximation and finite determinacy produce an algebraic local ring with the same completed local ring as the analytic singularity. Completion records all formal infinitesimal orders around the point. The manuscript keeps the equations and their relations together, then uses a Jacobian presentation and faithful flatness to descend freeness of derivations. Shrinking to one affine neighborhood gives the globally free module asserted in Theorem 1.1.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The claimed surface is affine and noncompact. It does not contradict the compact classification result identifying compact complex surfaces with globally free rank-two tangent sheaf as complex tori.

Its tangent frame cannot be chosen commuting near the singular point, by the earlier commuting-frame theorem. A reader should therefore not interpret the two generators as the partial derivatives of a hidden coordinate chart.

The example also lies outside the known complete-intersection, graded-cone, and log-canonical affirmative settings. Its construction does not provide a universal classification of singularities with free tangent sheaf or a minimal possible value of the local geometric genus.

The derivation-blowup consequence is restricted to that prescribed operation. General resolution methods remain available in characteristic zero. A natural further question is which additional information about vector-field brackets or differential forms restores an effective smoothness criterion.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Theorem 1.1 gives the algebraic endpoint. Sections 2–5 construct the analytic germ, Remark 5.5 records its resolution invariants, and Section 6 explains algebraization and the two further consequences.

The primary papers linked in Section 3 describe the earlier affirmative cases. Optional background on derivations and regular local rings helps connect the statement to ordinary differentiation and the algebraic definition of a smooth point.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf (September 23, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 050 — Ample bundles without Griffiths-positive metrics on the quadric
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 050 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

Algebraic geometry and differential geometry have different ways to say that a bundle is positive. Algebraic positivity asks whether enough sections eventually give a projective embedding. Differential positivity asks whether a metric has positive curvature in specified directions.

For line bundles on a smooth projective variety, these viewpoints agree. Griffiths’ conjecture asks whether the same is true for vector bundles: must an ample holomorphic vector bundle admit a smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive curvature?

Family 050 contains one manuscript claiming counterexamples of rank two on the quadric surface P1×P1\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1P1×P1. Every member of its explicit family is ample, but all sufficiently large members are asserted to admit no metric of the required kind.

The manuscript credits an earlier 2026 counterexample of Du–Xie on an abelian surface. Its contribution is a different construction on a rational surface, an explicit family with quantified algebraic positivity, and a limiting obstruction applying to every smooth strictly positive Hermitian metric on the indicated members.

2. Background and essential definitions

Bundles and metrics

A rank-two holomorphic vector bundle EEE attaches a copy of C2\mathbb C^2C2 to every point of a complex manifold, with holomorphic changes of coordinates between local trivializations. A Hermitian metric is a smoothly varying positive-definite Hermitian inner product on those fibers.

In a local frame, its squared norm has the form

∥v∥h2=∑α,β=12hαβˉ(x)vαvβ‾.\|v\|_h^2=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=1}^{2}h_{\alpha\bar\beta}(x)v_\alpha\overline{v_\beta}.∥v∥h2​=α,β=1∑2​hαβˉ​​(x)vα​vβ​​.

The dependence on the fiber variable vvv is quadratic. This restriction will matter: more general homogeneous norms, called complex Finsler metrics, need not arise from an inner product.

The Hermitian metric determines the Chern connection, whose curvature records how the fiber geometry varies around infinitesimal loops in the base. Strict Griffiths positivity requires a positive curvature value for every nonzero base tangent direction ξ\xiξ and every nonzero fiber vector vvv. In local coefficients, the condition is

∑j,k,α,βcjkˉαβˉξjξk‾vαvβ‾>0.\sum_{j,k,\alpha,\beta}c_{j\bar k\alpha\bar\beta}\xi_j\overline{\xi_k}v_\alpha\overline{v_\beta}>0.j,k,α,β∑​cjkˉαβˉ​​ξj​ξk​​vα​vβ​​>0.

Semipositivity replaces >0>0>0 by ≥0\ge0≥0. Excluding strictly positive metrics does not automatically exclude semipositive ones.

Ampleness for a vector bundle

Let P(E)\mathbb P(E)P(E) parametrize one-dimensional quotients of the fibers of EEE. It carries a tautological quotient line bundle OP(E)(1)\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E)}(1)OP(E)​(1). The vector bundle EEE is ample when this line bundle is ample, meaning some positive tensor power gives a projective embedding.

This definition tests the geometry of the projectivized bundle. It does not initially specify a quadratic norm on EEE itself. A strictly Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric implies ampleness; the conjecture asks for the converse.

A Finsler metric can have the homogeneity of a norm without the quadratic formula above. Positivity results allowing such metrics, or metrics on a determinant twist or symmetric power of EEE, are therefore not automatically statements about the original Hermitian problem.

The base and its power maps

The quadric surface is

S=P1×P1.S=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1.S=P1×P1.

Its two projections give two families of projective lines, called rulings. The line bundle OS(a,b)\mathcal O_S(a,b)OS​(a,b) has degree aaa along one ruling and bbb along the other. Put P=OS(1,1)P=\mathcal O_S(1,1)P=OS​(1,1), which is ample.

The map fm:S→Sf_m:S\to Sfm​:S→S raises homogeneous coordinates in each factor to their mmm-th powers. It is finite of degree m2m^2m2, and

fm∗P≃P⊗m.f_m^*P\simeq P^{\otimes m}.fm∗​P≃P⊗m.

Pullback changes the scale of the bundle’s geometry, while the family below adds only one fixed positive twist PPP.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Hartshorne’s theory of ample vector bundles organized algebraic positivity through symmetric powers, generation, and the tautological line bundle. Griffiths’ differential-geometric formulation asked for a bridge from such algebraic positivity to a curvature condition on a Hermitian metric.

The bridge is established for line bundles. It is also established for vector bundles on compact complex curves, through work of Umemura and Campana–Flenner, with later analytic approaches including Murakami’s work. Thus rank two and base dimension two are the first possible dimensions for the phenomenon claimed here.

Other positive results modify the bundle. Berndtsson proved Nakano positivity for E⊗det⁡EE\otimes\det EE⊗detE when EEE is ample. Nakano positivity is stronger than Griffiths positivity, but the determinant twist is part of the conclusion. Liu–Sun–Yang obtained further positivity statements for symmetric powers and determinant-twisted bundles. These results do not simply remove the twist and produce the conjectured metric on EEE.

Kobayashi characterized ampleness through negatively curved strongly pseudoconvex Finsler structures on the dual bundle. The freedom to use a nonquadratic norm is crucial. Demailly’s later analytic systems and curvature functionals sought to recover the more restrictive Hermitian structure.

A recent obstruction of Lempert concerns a prescribed equivariant rule for constructing a Hermitian metric from a tautological metric. As M1 notes, those examples still admit positive Hermitian metrics by other means. Failure of one construction rule is weaker than nonexistence of every positive metric.

Most directly, Du–Xie’s preprint of 22 September 2026 states an ample rank-two bundle on an abelian surface without any smooth Griffiths-semipositive Hermitian metric. M1 explicitly credits that earlier claim and gives a different family on the quadric, with the weaker metric exclusion of strict positivity.

A subsequent Liu–Wan preprint of 29 September 2026 states examples on every Hirzebruch surface with additional stability and a stronger Finsler-curvature exclusion. Its curvature condition is on the original bundle, whereas Kobayashi’s ampleness characterization uses negative curvature on the dual. These are related developments with different conclusions and constructions.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

Theorem 1.1 of M1 asserts an explicitly constructed rank-two algebraic bundle GGG on SSS for which

Em=fm∗G⊗PE_m=f_m^*G\otimes PEm​=fm∗​G⊗P

is ample for every positive integer mmm. It further claims an integer m0m_0m0​ such that for every m≥m0m\ge m_0m≥m0​, the bundle EmE_mEm​ has no smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive curvature.

The quantifiers differ on the two sides. Ampleness holds for all m≥1m\ge1m≥1; metric nonexistence is asserted for all sufficiently large mmm. The theorem does not identify which of the finitely many smaller values admit such metrics.

The ampleness statement comes with a numerical bound. Proposition 3.1 states that

OP(Em)(n)is very ample whenever n is even and n−1≥3m.\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_m)}(n)\quad\text{is very ample whenever }n\text{ is even and }n-1\ge3m.OP(Em​)​(n)is very ample whenever n is even and n−1≥3m.

“Very ample” means the line bundle itself supplies a projective embedding. This is a concrete statement about enough algebraic sections. In contrast, the threshold m0m_0m0​ is obtained by compactness and is ineffective: the manuscript gives no explicit numerical value.

The excluded metrics are smooth, Hermitian, and strictly Griffiths-positive. Singular metrics, semipositive metrics, nonquadratic Finsler structures, and metrics on modified bundles are different questions unless specifically addressed by another theorem.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5. If correct, the construction would exhibit a broad family separating algebraic ampleness from smooth Hermitian curvature positivity on a particularly simple surface.

The central conjecture already has an earlier counterexample claim credited in the source. This family’s significance is therefore its specific rational base, explicit pullback-and-twist construction, all-parameter ampleness bound, and general limiting argument. It should not be described as having sole priority for the negative answer.

The geometric lesson is substantial: plenty of sections of the tautological bundle need not organize themselves into a smoothly varying quadratic norm with positive curvature on the original vector bundle. Fiberwise quadratic structure is additional information, not a harmless choice of notation.

The result would also distinguish flexibility gained by determinant twists or Finsler norms from the original metric problem. Those positive theories can remain valid while the Hermitian converse fails.

6. The main idea

Encode incompatible symmetries in a bundle

Choose two projective transformations A,BA,BA,B of P1\mathbb P^1P1, each of order three, with no common fixed point, but such that their product acts, after a coordinate change, like

z⟼λz,∣λ∣>1.z\longmapsto\lambda z,\qquad |\lambda|>1.z⟼λz,∣λ∣>1.

The manuscript gives explicit matrix lifts and arranges finite orders for the relative lifts needed at graph intersections. Consider the three graphs of the identity, AAA, and BBB inside SSS.

The bundle GGG is built from pairs of sections of two line bundles, one positive along each ruling, required to agree along those graphs through prescribed identifications. This is an elementary transformation. Compatibility at intersections makes the construction locally free rather than merely a singular sheaf.

Two quotient-line-bundle sequences then control symmetric powers of GGG. Alternating their filtrations and adding the positive twist supplies the stated very-ampleness bound for every EmE_mEm​.

Positive metrics would produce a nonzero quadratic limit

Assume positive metrics exist for infinitely many mmm. Their dual squared norms are plurisubharmonic: restriction to every holomorphic disc has the subharmonic mean-value property.

M1 averages these norms over the finite power maps and normalizes them. The twisting factor becomes asymptotically negligible. Its compactness argument produces a finite nonnegative plurisubharmonic function on G∗G^*G∗ that is a Hermitian quadratic form on every fiber and is not identically zero.

The limit may lose rank, so it is permitted to be only a seminorm. What must survive is nonzero mass and quadratic behavior even over the graph divisor. An almost-everywhere statement alone would not retain the relations imposed there.

The limit would force an impossible invariant measure

On either dual line subbundle, compactness of the opposite projective-line direction forces the limiting seminorm to be independent of that direction. The graph identifications therefore produce one nonzero seminorm on a negative line bundle over P1\mathbb P^1P1, invariant under both AAA and BBB.

Taking curvature in the sense of distributions yields a finite positive measure of nonzero total mass. Invariance under the expanding product ABABAB forces that measure to be supported on its two fixed points: successive disjoint annuli otherwise all have the same positive mass, contradicting finiteness.

Both order-three transformations preserve this support. An order-three permutation of at most two points must fix each point, so they would have a common fixed point, contrary to their construction. This excludes the limiting quadratic object and hence excludes an infinite sequence of positive-metric parameters. Only finitely many small mmm can remain.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The theorem concerns the stated rank-two family on P1×P1\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1P1×P1. It does not assert that every ample rank-two bundle on that surface lacks positive metrics; direct sums of suitable positive line bundles provide familiar positive examples.

There is no explicit value of m0m_0m0​, so the claim does not identify a numerically specified first counterexample in the family. The explicit construction of GGG and the effective very-ampleness bound do not make the metric threshold effective.

Strict positivity is essential to the reported exclusion. The theorem should not be upgraded to nonexistence of semipositive Hermitian metrics or every Finsler structure by borrowing conclusions from different examples in the cited literature.

Natural further questions concern the smallest failing parameter, additional hypotheses restoring Hermitian positivity, and the exact relationship among algebraic positivity, singular metrics, and nonquadratic curvature conditions.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Theorem 1.1 states the family and threshold; Proposition 3.1 gives the very-ampleness bound; Proposition 4.1 gives the limiting quadratic object; Section 5 supplies the invariant-measure obstruction.

The primary historical sources linked above separate the curve theorem, twisted-bundle results, Finsler characterization, and recent counterexample claims. Background on Hermitian vector bundles helps with the metric language. The distinction between a quadratic Hermitian norm and a more general homogeneous norm is the key point throughout.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Ample rank-two bundles on the quadric surface without Griffiths-positive metrics (September 24, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 049 — Affine space embedded in a way coordinates cannot straighten
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 049 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

A copy of affine three-space can be described by a complicated equation inside affine four-space. Does its complicated appearance always disappear after a polynomial change of ambient coordinates?

The Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture predicts that a hypersurface isomorphic to affine space can be straightened into a coordinate hyperplane in characteristic zero. It concerns the embedding, not merely the abstract shape of the hypersurface.

Family 049 contains two manuscripts claiming explicit counterexamples in four variables. They demonstrate different phenomena. M1 gives a polynomial that is not a coordinate, becomes one after adding a single variable, and has every fiber isomorphic to affine three-space. M2 gives a different polynomial whose zero fiber is affine three-space but which has a critical point on another fiber.

The critical point makes M2’s obstruction easy to state and preserves it after adjoining any number of unused variables. M1 cannot use that obstruction: its stable-coordinate property requires a subtler argument involving additive group actions.

2. Background and essential definitions

Coordinates are global polynomial data

A polynomial f∈C[x1,…,xn]f\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]f∈C[x1​,…,xn​] is a coordinate if other polynomials complete it to a coordinate system:

C[x1,…,xn]=C[f,f2,…,fn].\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]=\mathbb C[f,f_2,\ldots,f_n].C[x1​,…,xn​]=C[f,f2​,…,fn​].

Equivalently, a polynomial automorphism carries fff to the first standard coordinate. An automorphism requires a polynomial inverse, not just a locally invertible or analytic change of variables.

For example, x+y2x+y^2x+y2 is a coordinate in two variables because the change (x,y)↦(x+y2,y)(x,y)\mapsto(x+y^2,y)(x,y)↦(x+y2,y) is inverted by (u,v)↦(u−v2,v)(u,v)\mapsto(u-v^2,v)(u,v)↦(u−v2,v). Every fiber is a parabola, and the same ambient automorphism straightens all of them at once.

A polynomial is one-stably a coordinate if it becomes a coordinate after adjoining one new independent variable. The Stable Coordinate Conjecture asks whether this can happen without the polynomial already being a coordinate.

An abstract fiber and its embedding

The fiber f−1(λ)f^{-1}(\lambda)f−1(λ) has coordinate ring

C[x1,…,xn]/(f−λ).\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f-\lambda).C[x1​,…,xn​]/(f−λ).

Saying this ring is polynomial in n−1n-1n−1 variables describes the fiber intrinsically. An isomorphism may use formulas that work only after the equation f=λf=\lambdaf=λ has been imposed.

The embedding is rectifiable if a polynomial automorphism of the entire ambient affine space carries the fiber to a coordinate hyperplane. Extending coordinates off the fiber is the extra requirement. Thus even a full polynomial parametrization of the hypersurface need not solve the embedding problem.

The Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture asks whether

C[x1,…,xn]/(f)≃C[t1,…,tn−1]⟹f is a coordinate.\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f)\simeq\mathbb C[t_1,\ldots,t_{n-1}]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f\text{ is a coordinate}.C[x1​,…,xn​]/(f)≃C[t1​,…,tn−1​]⟹f is a coordinate.

Critical points give one obstruction

A critical point of fff is a point where all partial derivatives vanish. A coordinate polynomial has no critical points: it is a row of the Jacobian matrix of a polynomial automorphism, and that matrix is invertible everywhere.

This gives a useful asymmetry. A critical point anywhere in the ambient space disproves coordinateness, even when it lies far from the zero fiber. The zero fiber can still be perfectly smooth and abstractly affine space.

This obstruction is unavailable when the polynomial becomes a coordinate after adding unused variables, since its zero derivatives in those new directions would leave any old critical point intact.

3. Development history and previous partial results

The two-variable embedding problem is solved affirmatively by the Abhyankar–Moh theorem and Suzuki’s related work: an affine line embedded as such a plane curve can be straightened.

In three variables, important positive results impose conditions on the equation or its general fiber. Sathaye treated planes defined by polynomials linear in one variable, and Russell extended that result to arbitrary fields. Kaliman proved that a polynomial on C3\mathbb C^3C3 with general fiber C2\mathbb C^2C2 is a coordinate. This does not resolve the full three-variable embedding question from a single affine-plane fiber.

Together with curve and surface cancellation, these results imply the Stable Coordinate Conjecture over C\mathbb CC in at most three original variables, as explained by Shpilrain–Yu. Four variables are therefore the first possible dimension for M1’s stable-coordinate counterexample.

The Vénéreau polynomials have been important candidates and testing grounds in four variables. Lewis proved that the second Vénéreau polynomial is a coordinate. Blanc–Poloni developed affine-bundle and bivariable methods, revisited that result, and established one-stability for a wider family. Exhibiting stable coordinates was thus already possible; ruling out every original coordinate system remained the separate challenge.

For the embedding problem in four variables, Kaliman–Vénéreau–Zaidenberg and Maubach proved affirmative results for equations of the form a(x)y+b(x,z,t)a(x)y+b(x,z,t)a(x)y+b(x,z,t), with the coefficient depending on only one variable. More recent work of Ghosh, Gupta, and Pal treats related linear hypersurfaces under further hypotheses. M2 is designed outside those restricted equation classes.

Shpilrain–Yu used ambient critical loci to distinguish inequivalent embeddings and asked whether an affine-space zero fiber forces the gradient to be nowhere zero. M2 claims a negative answer, while M1 claims an obstruction even with every fiber affine space.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

M1: degree five, all fibers affine, one stabilization sufficient

In four independent variables, put

Q=x22−x42+x1x3,f=x1−2Q(Q(x2+x4)+x1x4).Q=x_2^2-x_4^2+x_1x_3,\qquadf=x_1-2Q\bigl(Q(x_2+x_4)+x_1x_4\bigr).Q=x22​−x42​+x1​x3​,f=x1​−2Q(Q(x2​+x4​)+x1​x4​).

Theorem 1.1 of M1 claims that this degree-five polynomial is not a coordinate of C[x1,x2,x3,x4]\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]C[x1​,x2​,x3​,x4​], but becomes a coordinate after adjoining one variable www.

Corollary 1.2 states that for every λ∈C\lambda\in\mathbb Cλ∈C,

f−1(λ)≃A3,f^{-1}(\lambda)\simeq\mathbb A^3,f−1(λ)≃A3,

and that none of these embeddings in A4\mathbb A^4A4 is rectifiable. If any one fiber could be taken to a coordinate hyperplane, its prime principal ideal would be taken to the ideal of a coordinate. Its defining polynomial would differ from that coordinate by a nonzero constant factor, contradicting the asserted noncoordinateness of fff.

This simultaneously claims failure of stable coordinates in the smallest possible ambient dimension and failure of the embedding conjecture there.

M2: an affine zero fiber with a critical point elsewhere

Use four different independent variables h,u,v,wh,u,v,wh,u,v,w, and define

x=u3+hv,y=−u2+hw,x=u^3+hv,\qquad y=-u^2+hw,x=u3+hv,y=−u2+hw,
s=2u3v+3u4w+h(v2−3u2w2)+h2w3.s=2u^3v+3u^4w+h(v^2-3u^2w^2)+h^2w^3.s=2u3v+3u4w+h(v2−3u2w2)+h2w3.

These abbreviations satisfy x2+y3=hsx^2+y^3=hsx2+y3=hs. Set

p=−2s2x+3sy2−3s3y,F=h−p−1.p=-2s^2x+3sy^2-3s^3y,\qquad F=h-p-1.p=−2s2x+3sy2−3s3y,F=h−p−1.

Theorem 1.1 of M2 claims

C[h,u,v,w]/(F)≃C[t1,t2,t3],∇F(2,0,−1/2,1/2)=0.\mathbb C[h,u,v,w]/(F)\simeq\mathbb C[t_1,t_2,t_3],\qquad\nabla F(2,0,-1/2,1/2)=0.C[h,u,v,w]/(F)≃C[t1​,t2​,t3​],∇F(2,0,−1/2,1/2)=0.

The stated critical point lies on F=−1F=-1F=−1, not on the smooth zero fiber. Hence FFF is not a coordinate despite its affine-three-space zero fiber.

Adding independent variables preserves both the polynomial zero-fiber quotient and the critical point. M2 therefore claims embedding counterexamples in every ambient dimension at least four. In contrast, M1’s particular obstruction disappears after one added variable by design.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5. If correct, these examples would settle major affine-embedding and stable-coordinate questions negatively, with explicit formulas in the first possible dimension for stable-coordinate failure.

They expose three distinct levels of information: one fiber is affine space; every fiber is affine space; the polynomial is a coordinate. The claimed examples separate all the implications needed for the corresponding conjectures.

M2 would show that the intrinsic simplicity of one fiber says little about critical behavior elsewhere. M1 goes further in a different direction: even uniform affine-space fibers would fail to provide a single ambient coordinate system. Stabilization would erase that obstruction.

Neither manuscript needs an exotic ambient variety. The ambient space is ordinary A4\mathbb A^4A4; the complexity lies in how a distinguished polynomial organizes it.

6. The main idea

M1: coordinates on the ring need not include the chosen element

M1 presents a four-variable polynomial ring as a hypersurface in five variables, with a distinguished element ppp. A determinant-preserving matrix substitution makes the defining equation linear in a new variable. Eliminating that variable identifies the quotient with a polynomial ring and turns ppp into the displayed degree-five fff.

A second explicit substitution, using the exponential of a locally nilpotent derivation, makes ppp part of a coordinate system after one extra variable. A locally nilpotent derivation acts like differentiation along an algebraic additive-group action; its exponential terminates on every polynomial.

To obstruct coordinateness before stabilization, the manuscript places an integer-indexed filtration on the ring, including negative degrees. If ppp were a coordinate, differentiating in another coordinate would induce a prohibited additive action on a simpler graded algebra associated with an affine quadric.

A line-bundle lift makes a key ideal principal. The generator has a highest part factoring as (au−d)(au+d)(au-d)(au+d)(au−d)(au+d). The resulting invariance constraints force a coefficient to be both a polynomial in variables of nonnegative weight and an element of negative weight. M1 presents this incompatibility as the final obstruction. It adapts the method of family 047, but here the original ring itself is already polynomial.

M2: use a cusp relation to build the affine fiber

M2 starts with the cusp parametrization (u3,−u2)(u^3,-u^2)(u3,−u2), for which x2+y3=0x^2+y^3=0x2+y3=0, and perturbs both entries by multiples of hhh. The quotient of x2+y3x^2+y^3x2+y3 by hhh supplies sss.

On the zero fiber, the translation

X=x+s3,Y=y−s2X=x+s^3,\qquad Y=y-s^2X=x+s3,Y=y−s2

turns an auxiliary relation into s=X2+Y3s=X^2+Y^3s=X2+Y3. This identifies an auxiliary algebra with a polynomial ring in two variables. A lifting lemma supplies the third variable by solving compatible linear equations whose coefficients generate the unit ideal.

That unit-ideal condition is important: it allows polynomial formulas valid everywhere, without dividing by a coefficient that could vanish. The appendix records coordinates and their polynomial inverse for the entire zero fiber.

The noncoordinate conclusion then comes from the separately stated critical point in the original ambient four-space. The construction distinguishes a global parametrization of the zero fiber from a global automorphism of the ambient space.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

Both constructions are over C\mathbb CC. M1 concerns a one-stable coordinate in four original variables, and M2 concerns an affine zero fiber with a persistent critical-point obstruction. M2 is not a stable-coordinate example; adjoining unused variables cannot remove its critical point.

The family does not give an affine-space cancellation counterexample in dimension three. In M1 the ambient fourfold and every fiber are already affine spaces; what allegedly fails is rectification of the chosen polynomial. Cancellation and coordinate questions have relationships, but their negations cannot be exchanged without an argument.

The three-variable Abhyankar–Sathaye problem from a single affine-plane fiber is not addressed. The earlier affirmative special cases remain distinct from the four-variable counterexamples claimed here.

Further questions include identifying additional hypotheses on an affine-space fibration that force a coordinate, and understanding how stabilization changes the possible polynomial embeddings.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Theorem 1.1 gives the degree-five stable-coordinate claim and Corollary 1.2 its all-fibers consequence. M2’s Theorem 1.1 gives the zero-fiber isomorphism and critical point, while its appendix provides explicit inverse coordinate maps.

The primary works linked above trace the low-dimensional embedding theorems, Vénéreau examples, and critical-locus approach. The useful distinction throughout is between coordinates on a hypersurface and coordinates on its entire ambient affine space.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables (October 5, 2026).
  • M2. OpenAI, An explicit noncoordinate polynomial with affine three-space zero fibre (September 24, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 051 — Hyperbolicity forces an ample canonical bundle
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 051 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

A compact complex manifold is hyperbolic when holomorphic maps into it are strongly constrained. One concrete formulation says that every holomorphic map from the whole complex plane must be constant. Can this prohibition on curves force the manifold to have enough top-degree differential forms to embed in projective space?

Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture predicts that it can, for compact Kähler manifolds. The conclusion is about the canonical line bundle, which packages holomorphic forms of top degree. Its ampleness would connect an analytic restriction on one-dimensional maps with global algebraic positivity in every dimension.

Family 051 contains one manuscript claiming this implication for every smooth compact connected Kähler manifold of positive complex dimension. Projectivity is a conclusion, not an assumption. The claimed advance replaces a negative-curvature metric hypothesis from major earlier theorems by hyperbolicity itself.

2. Background and essential definitions

Entire curves and two notions of hyperbolicity

An entire curve in XXX is a holomorphic map C→X\mathbb C\to XC→X. It need not be an embedding, proper, or algebraic. A manifold is Brody hyperbolic if every such map is constant.

The Kobayashi pseudodistance is an intrinsic distance-like function built by joining holomorphic discs and measuring lengths using the hyperbolic geometry of the unit disc. It may assign distance zero to distinct points. Kobayashi hyperbolicity means it is a genuine distance.

Brody’s theorem makes these two conditions equivalent for compact complex manifolds. Compactness is essential to this equivalence as used here. Throughout this digest, hyperbolicity refers to that compact setting.

A compact hyperbolic manifold contains neither rational nor elliptic curves. A nonconstant map from either kind of curve would yield a nonconstant entire curve after using the usual plane parametrization or universal cover. The converse is false: ruling out only rational curves is a substantially weaker requirement.

The canonical bundle

For a complex nnn-fold, the canonical bundle is

KX=⋀n(T1,0X)∗.K_X=\bigwedge^n(T^{1,0}X)^*.KX​=⋀n​(T1,0X)∗.

Locally its sections are expressions f(z) dz1∧⋯∧dznf(z)\,dz_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dz_nf(z)dz1​∧⋯∧dzn​. Sections of KX⊗mK_X^{\otimes m}KX⊗m​ are called pluricanonical forms. If sufficiently many of them separate points and tangent directions, they define a projective embedding.

A line bundle is ample if some positive power defines such an embedding. It is nef if its curvature can be made arbitrarily close to nonnegative, allowing an arbitrarily small negative error relative to a fixed Kähler form. It is big if its spaces of sections grow at the maximal rate proportional to mnm^nmn.

These are different properties. Nefness can occur with zero top self-intersection and very few sections. Bigness supplies many sections, but does not alone guarantee an embedding everywhere. Ampleness is the desired final conclusion.

A curve provides the model

For a compact Riemann surface of genus ggg,

deg⁡KX=2g−2.\deg K_X=2g-2.degKX​=2g−2.

The hyperbolic cases have g≥2g\ge2g≥2, so the canonical bundle has positive degree and is ample. The conjecture asks for a higher-dimensional analogue without assuming a uniformizing disc or a particular negatively curved metric in advance.

A Kähler manifold has a positive closed differential two-form compatible with its complex structure. This is a strong geometric condition, but it does not by itself imply that the manifold is projective.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Kobayashi’s intrinsic metric theory and Brody’s compactness theorem established the connection between entire curves and hyperbolicity. The canonical-ampleness question asks how that analytic notion interacts with birational and projective geometry.

A major advance was Wu–Yau’s theorem: a smooth projective manifold with a Kähler metric of negative holomorphic sectional curvature has ample canonical bundle. Holomorphic sectional curvature measures curvature along complex tangent lines.

Tosatti–Yang extended this conclusion to compact Kähler manifolds without assuming projectivity. Diverio–Trapani treated quasi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature, where curvature is nonpositive everywhere and strictly negative in every nonzero tangent direction at one point. Further work allows certain Hermitian metrics while retaining a Kähler ambient manifold.

These results provide crucial analytic precedents, but negative curvature is additional structure. The absence of entire curves does not hand us a smooth metric with the curvature inequalities those arguments use. Removing that extra hypothesis is the gap addressed by M1.

Another affirmative theory uses Kähler hyperbolicity in Gromov’s sense: a Kähler form becomes the exterior derivative of a bounded one-form on the universal cover. Gromov established general-type consequences, and Chen–Yang proved canonical ampleness under that hypothesis. This is a distinct definition and must not be substituted for Brody hyperbolicity merely because both names include “hyperbolic.”

Nefness is also a different, weaker stage of the problem. M1 credits Ou’s uniruledness characterization and Cao–Höring’s rational-curve theorem with giving nefness of the canonical bundle when a compact Kähler manifold contains no rational curves. The further difficulty is to force positive canonical volume and then ampleness.

M1 proposes to obtain that missing quantitative positivity directly from extremal holomorphic discs, using derivative bounds supplied by compact hyperbolicity.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

Theorem 1.1 states that if XXX is compact, connected, Kähler, and of complex dimension n≥1n\ge1n≥1, then

every holomorphic C→X is constant⟹KX is ample.\text{every holomorphic }\mathbb C\to X\text{ is constant}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_X\text{ is ample}.every holomorphic C→X is constant⟹KX​ is ample.

In particular, some positive power of KXK_XKX​ defines a holomorphic embedding into complex projective space. The conclusion includes projectivity even when none was assumed initially.

The theorem imposes no prescribed curvature bound on a chosen metric and no restriction to a known class of projective examples. It is stated for smooth manifolds; singular spaces require separate formulations.

Consequences using other manuscript claims

Corollary 10.1 combines canonical ampleness with the Fujita freeness claim in family 038 to state that

KX⊗m is globally generated for every m≥n+2.K_X^{\otimes m}\text{ is globally generated for every }m\ge n+2.KX⊗m​ is globally generated for every m≥n+2.

Global generation means that at every point some section is nonzero. It does not mean that this particular power necessarily gives an embedding; separating points and tangent directions is stronger.

Corollary 10.2 adds an extra assumption: the ordinary universal cover is biholomorphic to a semialgebraic open subset of a projective variety. Semialgebraic means described in affine charts by finitely many real polynomial equalities and inequalities, combined by Boolean operations.

Using the classification claimed in family 058, M1 then obtains a connected finite unramified cover of XXX of the form

(D/Γ0)×F.(D/\Gamma_0)\times F.(D/Γ0​)×F.

Here DDD is a bounded symmetric domain, Γ0\Gamma_0Γ0​ acts freely and cocompactly, and FFF is a simply connected compact hyperbolic projective manifold. Either factor may be a point. Neither companion result is used in the principal canonical-ampleness argument.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 5/5. If correct, the theorem would settle a central conjecture linking complex hyperbolicity to algebraic positivity in the smooth compact Kähler category.

Its hypothesis concerns only holomorphic maps from a one-dimensional noncompact source. Its conclusion produces a positive line bundle governing the entire manifold and an embedding into projective space. This is a strong bridge between analysis and algebraic geometry.

The distinction from earlier negative-curvature theorems is substantial. A theorem from hyperbolicity alone would apply without first solving a separate metric-existence problem. It would also turn projectivity into a consequence of the analytic restriction.

The statement has one direction. It does not say that every manifold with ample canonical bundle is hyperbolic; positive canonical geometry does not automatically exclude every entire curve. Retaining this direction is essential to understanding both its strength and its limits.

6. The main idea

Replace curvature assumptions with an extremal-disc problem

Fix a background Kähler metric kkk on XXX. Compact hyperbolicity supplies a uniform upper bound DDD for the squared norm of the derivative at the center of every holomorphic unit disc.

M1 considers discs with a fixed center and finite area. It maximizes a functional combining the central derivative, a weighted integral of a closed two-form, and a negative area penalty. The penalty controls escape in the optimization problem.

The difficult point is the boundary. Convergence on compact subsets of the open disc does not automatically justify differentiating an integral over the whole disc. The manuscript first obtains boundary regularity from maximality, then constructs a holomorphic frame normalized on the boundary and actual variations that keep the disc’s center fixed.

One Hessian identity supplies two estimates

For a Kähler metric hhh, write its Ricci form as

Rh=−i∂∂ˉlog⁡det⁡h.R_h=-i\partial\bar\partial\log\det h.Rh​=−i∂∂ˉlogdeth.

M1 computes the sum of second derivatives of the area functional along its special variations. The resulting identity relates that Hessian to the integral of RhR_hRh​.

One choice of parameters supplies bounded canonical potentials and hence nefness. A second gives the stated pointwise estimate

hn≥e−D(n2n+D)nknwhenever Rh≥−h.h^n\ge e^{-D}\left(\frac{n}{2n+D}\right)^n k^n\qquad\text{whenever }R_h\ge-h.hn≥e−D(2n+Dn​)nknwhenever Rh​≥−h.

The forms hnh^nhn and knk^nkn are volume forms. The inequality says a whole family of qualifying metrics cannot collapse its volume density to zero, with the bound controlled by the fixed background data. The conclusion is quantitative even though the optimizing discs themselves can vary with the metric.

Convert a volume lower bound into algebraic positivity

Following the Monge–Ampère strategy used in the earlier Wu–Yau theory, M1 solves for metrics hth_tht​ in the classes

2πc1(KX)+t[k],t>0,2\pi c_1(K_X)+t[k],\qquad t>0,2πc1​(KX​)+t[k],t>0,

with Rht=−ht+tkR_{h_t}=-h_t+tkRht​​=−ht​+tk. The volume estimate persists as ttt tends to zero and gives

∫Xc1(KX)n>0.\int_Xc_1(K_X)^n>0.∫X​c1​(KX​)n>0.

Together with nefness, established holomorphic Morse inequalities make KXK_XKX​ big. Its sections then make XXX Moishezon, meaning it has as many algebraically independent meromorphic functions as its dimension. A compact Kähler Moishezon manifold is projective.

Finally, established cone-theorem arguments use the absence of rational curves to upgrade the canonical positivity to ampleness. The manuscript’s new analytic estimate is intended to supply the missing positive-volume step; the later passage through bigness and projectivity uses existing results.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

Compactness and the Kähler condition are explicit hypotheses. The theorem does not assert the same conclusion for arbitrary noncompact hyperbolic manifolds or all compact non-Kähler manifolds. Boundary geometry changes the appropriate positivity question in the noncompact case.

Hyperbolicity means no nonconstant entire curves, not merely no rational curves. The weaker condition supports nefness in the cited theory but does not supply the full conclusion here.

The theorem also does not construct a metric of negative holomorphic sectional curvature from hyperbolicity. Its analytic method seeks canonical positivity directly, so it should not be reported as settling that stronger metric-existence question.

The effective global-generation exponent uses family 038, and the finite-cover product uses family 058 plus the additional semialgebraic hypothesis. Neither is an unconditional classification of all compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds. The general structure of such manifolds and their universal covers remains a broader problem.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Theorem 1.1 gives canonical ampleness. Sections 3–7 explain the disc optimization, boundary variations, and two estimates; Sections 8–9 make the transition to projective geometry. Section 10 labels the two companion-dependent consequences separately.

The primary papers linked above trace the negative-curvature and rational-curve predecessors. Optional background on the Kobayashi metric and canonical bundle helps connect the analytic hypothesis to the algebraic conclusion.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Canonical ampleness of compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds (September 23, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 052 — From a split tangent bundle to a product of manifolds
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 052 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

On a product Y1×Y2Y_1\times Y_2Y1​×Y2​, a tangent vector naturally splits into a direction along the first factor and a direction along the second. Suppose a complex manifold has exactly such a splitting at every point. Must the manifold itself come from a product?

There are two obstacles. First, the chosen directions must fit together into leaves, like coordinate slices. Second, local slices must continue globally without twisting or breaking down. Passing to the universal cover removes loop monodromy, but does not automatically solve the continuation problem.

Family 052 contains two complementary claims. M1 starts with two integrable tangent summands on a compact Kähler manifold and claims a compatible product decomposition of its ordinary universal cover. M2 starts with a rationally connected projective manifold and claims that every two-summand holomorphic splitting is automatically integrable. An earlier theorem then supplies a product of the original manifold itself.

In both statements, compatibility means preserving the particular tangent subbundles supplied at the start. An unrelated abstract product decomposition would not answer the question.

2. Background and essential definitions

Splitting directions and integrating them

The holomorphic tangent bundle TXT_XTX​ consists of the complex tangent spaces of XXX. A specified splitting

TX=E1⊕E2T_X=E_1\oplus E_2TX​=E1​⊕E2​

means each EiE_iEi​ is a holomorphic subbundle and every tangent vector has a unique decomposition into the two summands. Let their positive ranks be r1,r2r_1,r_2r1​,r2​, so dim⁡CX=r1+r2\dim_{\mathbb C}X=r_1+r_2dimC​X=r1​+r2​.

A subbundle EEE is integrable if the Lie bracket of any two local vector fields tangent to EEE is again tangent to EEE. The bracket measures the infinitesimal failure of successive motions to commute. Frobenius’ theorem says integrability is precisely the condition for local submanifolds tangent to the chosen directions to exist.

These local submanifolds fit together into leaves. If both complementary summands are integrable, local coordinates can be separated into two blocks, with one block varying along each leaf. Locally the manifold is a product. The global question remains.

Compatibility is stronger than being a product

An isomorphism X≃Y1×Y2X\simeq Y_1\times Y_2X≃Y1​×Y2​ is compatible with the specified splitting when it identifies EiE_iEi​ with the tangent directions of YiY_iYi​:

Ei≃pr⁡i∗TYiE_i\simeq\operatorname{pr}_i^*T_{Y_i}Ei​≃pri∗​TYi​​

as the actual subbundles of the tangent bundle, not only as abstract vector bundles.

Even a manifold already known to be a product can carry a different, nonintegrable tangent splitting. The manuscript recalls an example on an abelian surface times P1\mathbb P^1P1: adding noncommuting vertical vector fields to two translation directions gives a complementary subbundle whose bracket leaves that subbundle. Product topology alone does not force the specified directions to be product directions.

Covering spaces and rational curves

The ordinary universal cover X~→X\widetilde X\to XX→X is the simply connected topological covering equipped with its lifted complex structure. A product upstairs need not descend to a product downstairs: deck transformations can act on both factors together. Even a finite cover need not remove all such coupling.

A smooth projective variety is rationally connected if two general points lie on a rational curve, the image of P1\mathbb P^1P1. “General” means pairs in a nonempty algebraic open subset of X×XX\times XX×X. This is stronger than uniruledness, which requires a rational curve through a general individual point.

Rational connectedness supplies many moving rational curves and, in the smooth complex projective setting, simple connectedness. M2 uses this abundance of curves to control the Lie brackets of the tangent summands.

3. Development history and previous partial results

The Riemannian analogue is de Rham’s decomposition theorem: parallel orthogonal distributions on a complete Riemannian manifold give a product on its universal cover. A holomorphic splitting is weaker. Compactness makes a chosen metric complete, but does not make its given tangent subbundles parallel.

Beauville formulated the compatible splitting problem and proved major cases, including Kähler–Einstein manifolds and compact Kähler surfaces. For multiple summands, the compatible formulation involves integrability of relevant partial sums. In the two-summand setting here, integrability of both summands is the required local hypothesis.

Druel treated projective manifolds whose tangent bundle is a sum of line bundles. Brunella–Pereira–Touzet established splitting when one summand is a line bundle and its complement is integrable. Further work of Pereira–Touzet and Druel–Pereira–Pym–Touzet supplies product decompositions under flatness assumptions or the existence of a compact leaf with finite holonomy.

On the projective side, Höring proved automatic integrability for non-uniruled manifolds with split tangent bundle. He also proved that on a rationally connected projective manifold, integrability of one summand already gives a compatible product. The remaining rationally connected problem was therefore to force integrability without extra hypotheses.

Campana–Peternell obtained important low-rank Fano cases. Höring’s 2026 Fano-type theorem establishes algebraic integrability in a broad singular setting with Fano-type positivity, and gives an actual compatible product for smooth Fano manifolds. M2 claims to remove that positivity restriction in the smooth rationally connected case, with arbitrary positive ranks.

The family thus addresses two different missing steps: M1 globalizes an already integrable local product in general compact Kähler geometry; M2 supplies integrability from rational connectedness.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

M1: a compatible product on the universal cover

Let XXX be a compact connected Kähler manifold of dimension at least two, and assume both positive-rank summands in TX=E1⊕E2T_X=E_1\oplus E_2TX​=E1​⊕E2​ are integrable. M1 claims connected simply connected complex manifolds Y1,Y2Y_1,Y_2Y1​,Y2​ and a biholomorphism

Φ:X~→ ∼ Y1×Y2\Phi:\widetilde X\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Y_1\times Y_2Φ:X ∼ ​Y1​×Y2​

such that

dΦ(π∗Ei)=pr⁡i∗TYi,dim⁡CYi=ri.d\Phi(\pi^*E_i)=\operatorname{pr}_i^*T_{Y_i},\qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}Y_i=r_i.dΦ(π∗Ei​)=pri∗​TYi​​,dimC​Yi​=ri​.

Here π\piπ is the covering map. The factors are the universal covers of the intrinsic leaves through a common point. They can be noncompact, and the leaves use their own manifold topology.

Combining this with Höring’s earlier integrability theorem gives the same universal-cover conclusion for every two-summand splitting on a smooth non-uniruled projective manifold.

When KXK_XKX​ is nef and big, M1 also claims that the canonical Kähler–Einstein connection preserves the specified summands on the regular canonical locus. This is the inverse image of the smooth part of the canonical model under the pluricanonical contraction. Nefness means nonnegative degree on every curve; bigness means maximal growth of pluricanonical sections. The additional parallelism is more than the product conclusion already obtained from the non-uniruled case.

M2: rational connectedness forces integrability

For a smooth connected rationally connected projective complex manifold, M2 claims that both summands of every specified holomorphic splitting into two positive-rank subbundles are integrable, with no further rank or positivity condition.

Applying Höring’s established product theorem then yields

X≃X1×X2,Ei=pr⁡i∗TXi,X\simeq X_1\times X_2,\qquad E_i=\operatorname{pr}_i^*T_{X_i},X≃X1​×X2​,Ei​=pri∗​TXi​​,

where both factors are smooth projective manifolds. This is a product of XXX itself, stronger than an upstairs statement for a general compact Kähler manifold.

M2 also applies the result to general fibers of the rationally connected quotient of a uniruled compact Kähler manifold. It supplies integrability of the induced summands there, allowing earlier structure theorems to produce almost-holomorphic fibrations in the corresponding rational directions. When one ambient summand has rank two, those directions have rank two, one, or zero; the resulting conclusions differ accordingly. This is not an assertion that every uniruled manifold with a splitting is a global product.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5. If correct, the family would resolve the two-summand compatible splitting problem under its integrability hypothesis and a central automatic-integrability case beyond known positivity or rank restrictions.

Tangent bundles describe infinitesimal geometry. A theorem recovering a global product from their decomposition turns local linear information into a structural classification tool. Compatibility ensures that the factors explain the original geometry rather than merely provide another way to write the same space.

The complementary hypotheses are useful in different regions of the classification. Rationally connected varieties have many rational curves; non-uniruled varieties do not. M2 uses the former abundance, while M1 combines with earlier work in the latter setting. Neither manuscript erases the separate difficulties for general intermediate uniruled geometry.

6. The main idea

M1: continue rectangles, not just individual paths

With integrable complementary directions, a local map of two complex variables can move in E1E_1E1​ along the first variable and in E2E_2E2​ along the second. M1 calls such a map a holomorphic box. It need not be injective or have full rank.

The manuscript first extends these maps across Hartogs figures, domains in several complex variables where analytic continuation can fill a missing region. A general meromorphic extension could have indeterminacy; the separate tangent conditions are used to exclude the exceptional behavior and make the extension holomorphic.

It then crosses mixed boundaries using area estimates from a Kähler form. Closedness of that form permits Stokes’ theorem, while bounded projections onto the two summands control the relevant directions. No assumption that a metric already makes the summands parallel or orthogonal is introduced.

These extensions combine two disc axes into a whole box and preserve additional holomorphic parameters. Finite grids then combine continuous leafwise paths into rectangles. Continuing both the local product map and its inverse, and passing to simply connected covers, is intended to produce the global compatible biholomorphism.

M2: use rational curves to kill the bracket obstruction

M2 begins without integrability. Given a rational curve g:P1→Xg:\mathbb P^1\to Xg:P1→X, it claims a tangent-adapted map

F:P1×P1⟶X,F(s,s)=g(s),F:\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\longrightarrow X,\qquad F(s,s)=g(s),F:P1×P1⟶X,F(s,s)=g(s),

whose two factor directions map into E1E_1E1​ and E2E_2E2​. The construction starts formally near the diagonal, reconstructs a rational map using section counts, and removes indeterminacy through the tangent identities.

On this box, the pullback of each summand comes from its corresponding factor. Along a factor curve, the complementary summand is therefore trivial. This is the geometric feature needed to test integrability in arbitrary rank.

Failure of integrability is measured by the projected bracket tensor

⋀2Ei⟶Ej,j≠i.\bigwedge^2E_i\longrightarrow E_j,\qquad j\ne i.⋀2​Ei​⟶Ej​,j=i.

Rational connectedness supplies moving curves and sections vanishing at one marked point while spanning the desired tangent directions at another. Applying the bracket tensor gives a section of a trivial bundle on P1\mathbb P^1P1. Such a section is constant; because it vanishes at the first point, it vanishes at the second. The spanning property then forces the tensor to vanish on an open set, and holomorphicity extends the vanishing everywhere.

This separates the construction valid for split bundles from the final step where rational connectedness is essential.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

M1 assumes integrability. It does not claim that every holomorphic splitting on every compact Kähler manifold is integrable; the recalled product example shows why that would be false.

M1 concludes a product of the ordinary universal cover, not necessarily of XXX or a finite cover. M2’s actual product conclusion uses smooth rational connectedness and the earlier product theorem. Singular rationally connected spaces are not covered, and the source cites singular examples where automatic integrability fails.

Both main statements are formulated for two summands. More elaborate splittings require attention to integrability of partial sums; they should not be treated as an automatic restatement with more symbols.

The claims do not classify the individual factors or guarantee compact leaves in M1. Understanding intermediate uniruled cases and the possible deck-group actions remains part of the wider structure problem.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Theorem 1.1 is the integrable universal-cover statement; its corollaries and Section 7 give the projective and canonical-metric applications. M2’s Theorem 1.1 is automatic integrability, Corollary 1.2 invokes Höring for the actual product, and Section 5 states the rational-quotient consequences.

The primary works of Beauville and Höring linked above explain the conjectures and earlier cases. Background on foliations and the Frobenius theorem helps interpret integrability as the passage from directions to local slices.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, Universal-cover splitting for compact Kähler manifolds (September 23, 2026).
  • M2. OpenAI, Integrability of split tangent bundles on rationally connected manifolds (September 23, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 053 — A relation beyond Pixton’s original system
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 053 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 4/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

A ring can be described by generators and relations. Giving many true relations is useful; proving that they are all the relations is a much stronger achievement. The distinction is central to the intersection theory of moduli spaces of curves.

These moduli spaces carry natural geometric classes associated with marked points, differential forms, and degenerations into nodal curves. Pixton proposed a uniform graph-based system of relations among them. The relations are known to be valid. The completeness conjecture says that every relation among these natural classes follows from that system.

Family 053 contains one manuscript claiming a counterexample to completeness. It constructs a formal expression that becomes zero as an algebraic cycle but is not generated by the original Pixton relations, even after their standard gluing, forgetting, and multiplication consequences are included.

The example has extraordinarily large parameters. Its role is to disprove a universal assertion, not to provide a small relation ready for everyday computation.

2. Background and essential definitions

A space whose points are curves

The moduli space Mg,n\mathcal M_{g,n}Mg,n​ parametrizes smooth complex curves of genus ggg with nnn distinct labelled marked points. Its stable compactification M‾g,n\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}Mg,n​ also includes connected curves with ordinary nodes, where two branches cross.

Stability requires only finitely many automorphisms preserving the markings. For example, each rational component needs at least three special points, counting both markings and node branches. The condition 2g−2+n>02g-2+n>02g−2+n>0 gives the stable range.

The natural object is a moduli stack, which remembers finite automorphism groups. For this digest, one can think of an orbifold-like parameter space with rational coefficients accounting for those symmetries. Its complex dimension is

3g−3+n.3g-3+n.3g−3+n.

Boundary strata describe the different ways a curve can break into components. A stable graph records them: vertices represent components and their genera, edges represent nodes, and labelled legs represent markings.

Natural classes and their relations

At the iii-th marked point, the cotangent line has a first Chern class ψi\psi_iψi​. Other classes, called κ\kappaκ-classes, arise by forgetting a marking and pushing forward powers of a cotangent class. Together with boundary gluing operations, they generate the tautological ring.

The ambient Chow ring consists of algebraic cycles modulo rational equivalence, with multiplication given by intersection. We use rational coefficients. A codimension-ddd cycle also has a cohomology class in degree 2d2d2d, but different Chow classes can have the same cohomology class.

To keep formulas separate from their geometric values, introduce a strata algebra Sg,n\mathcal S_{g,n}Sg,n​. Its elements are formal linear combinations of decorated stable graphs, with the standard dimension truncations. Realizing a graph as its geometric boundary class gives a map

qg,n:Sg,n⟶A∗(M‾g,n;Q).q_{g,n}:\mathcal S_{g,n}\longrightarrowA^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n};\mathbb Q).qg,n​:Sg,n​⟶A∗(Mg,n​;Q).

The image is the tautological ring. The kernel consists of formal expressions that vanish geometrically: exactly the relations one wants to understand.

Validity and completeness

Let Pg,n\mathcal P_{g,n}Pg,n​ be Pixton’s original relation span, including its stated formal consequences. Validity means

Pg,n⊆ker⁡qg,n.\mathcal P_{g,n}\subseteq\ker q_{g,n}.Pg,n​⊆kerqg,n​.

Completeness means equality. A counterexample must do two things for the same formal class YYY: show qg,n(Y)=0q_{g,n}(Y)=0qg,n​(Y)=0, and show Y∉Pg,nY\notin\mathcal P_{g,n}Y∈/Pg,n​. Showing only that a new-looking formula vanishes is insufficient; it might already be a complicated combination of known relations.

3. Development history and previous partial results

Mumford initiated the systematic intersection-theoretic study of natural classes on moduli spaces of curves. Faber’s calculations and geometric constructions led to conjectural descriptions of the tautological ring on the smooth unpointed space Mg\mathcal M_gMg​.

Faber–Zagier supplied explicit hypergeometric relations among κ\kappaκ-classes. Pandharipande–Pixton proved those relations in Chow using stable quotients. The compactification requires additional boundary information, developed through the gluing and forgetting calculus of Arbarello–Cornalba and Graber–Pandharipande. In genus zero, Keel gave a presentation of the whole Chow ring by boundary divisors.

Pixton’s 2012 formula extended the relation system to stable pointed curves through decorated graphs and proposed completeness. Pandharipande–Pixton–Zvonkine proved cohomological validity using three-spin cohomological field theory. Janda proved Chow validity through equivariant Gromov–Witten theory of the projective line.

These are validity theorems: they establish that the proposed expressions vanish. They do not automatically identify the entire kernel of the realization map. Likewise, Janda’s comparison of relations produced by certain semisimple field-theory reconstructions compares those methods with Pixton’s system, not every possible source of Chow relations.

A nearby question asks whether the tautological ring is Gorenstein, meaning its multiplication pairings in complementary degrees are nondegenerate in the proposed manner. That is logically different from completeness. Pixton’s September 2026 paper proves that the tautological ring of M25\mathcal M_{25}M25​ is not Gorenstein while also establishing Faber–Zagier completeness there. Other compact-type examples similarly separate the two properties.

M1 therefore targets the original full relation span directly on the stable compactification. It does not infer incompleteness merely from a failure of duality in the ring.

4. What the new manuscripts claim

The parameters and the two conclusions

Set

g=1060,D∗=(g3),n=3D∗.g=10^{60},\qquad D_*={g\choose3},\qquad n=3D_*.g=1060,D∗​=(3g​),n=3D∗​.

Theorem 1.1 of M1 claims an explicitly defined class

Y∈Sg,n2D∗Y\in\mathcal S_{g,n}^{2D_*}Y∈Sg,n2D∗​​

for which

qg,n(Y)=0,Y∉Pg,n.q_{g,n}(Y)=0,\qquad Y\notin\mathcal P_{g,n}.qg,n​(Y)=0,Y∈/Pg,n​.

The superscript is codimension. It lies below the dimension 3g−3+n3g-3+n3g−3+n, so the assertion is not simply vanishing because the requested degree exceeds the dimension of the moduli space.

The same class yields a cohomological counterexample in degree 4D∗4D_*4D∗​. The cycle-class map sends its Chow realization to zero, while formal nonmembership in Pg,n\mathcal P_{g,n}Pg,n​ remains unchanged. This implication needs no injectivity of the cycle-class map: Chow vanishing already implies cohomological vanishing.

What “explicit” means at this scale

The construction uses ggg colors. For each increasing triple of colors, it allocates three labelled slots, producing n=3(g3)n=3{g\choose3}n=3(3g​) slots in total.

For a three-slot block J=(a,b,c)J=(a,b,c)J=(a,b,c), the manuscript combines two rational-tail divisor sums and a correction supported on rational bridges:

FJst=D‾ab D‾ac−12βJst.F_J^{\mathrm{st}}=\overline D_{ab}\,\overline D_{ac}-\frac12\beta_J^{\mathrm{st}}.FJst​=Dab​Dac​−21​βJst​.

Here D‾ab\overline D_{ab}Dab​ sums boundary divisors cutting off a genus-zero tail containing a,ba,ba,b. The bridge class βJst\beta_J^{\mathrm{st}}βJst​ inserts a genus-zero component carrying the three labels into an edge, giving two nodes, with specified graph-automorphism coefficients and forgetting pullbacks.

M1 multiplies one factor for every color triple and alternates over all relabelings preserving each slot’s color:

Y=∑τ preserves colorssgn⁡(τ) τ(∏JFJst).Y=\sum_{\tau\text{ preserves colors}}\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\,\tau\left(\prod_JF_J^{\mathrm{st}}\right).Y=τ preserves colors∑​sgn(τ)τ(J∏​FJst​).

Every operation is finite, though the expression is immense. The formula specifies a class without listing all of its terms. “Cubic” in the manuscript refers to its three marked inputs; each factor has Chow codimension two.

5. Why the advance matters

Importance: 4/5. If correct, this would disprove a central completeness proposal in the intersection theory of moduli spaces, in both rational Chow and rational cohomology.

The existing Pixton relations would remain true and useful. What changes is the belief that their formal closure accounts for every tautological relation. A missing relation would require a broader presentation of the ring or additional geometric principles generating relations.

The scale of the example affects practical usefulness but not the logic. A universal statement covering all genera and all marking counts fails if even one finite pair fails. The manuscript makes no claim that 106010^{60}1060 is close to the smallest possible genus.

The proposed mechanism is also informative: a formal algebra can satisfy all the tested graph relations while lacking a further identity forced by actual Chow correspondences. This would distinguish formal consistency with a relation system from geometric realizability.

6. The main idea

Use different tools for nonmembership and vanishing

M1 deliberately separates the two required conclusions. To show nonmembership, it constructs a linear detector on formal decorated graphs. To show vanishing, it uses actual algebraic cycles in families of curves and surfaces.

A detector is analogous to a linear functional that vanishes on a subspace but not on a candidate vector. If ℓ\ellℓ vanishes on every element of Pg,n\mathcal P_{g,n}Pg,n​ and ℓ(Y)≠0\ell(Y)\ne0ℓ(Y)=0, then YYY cannot belong to that span. This is an algebraic obstruction to derivability, rather than an attempt to enumerate all possible combinations of relations.

A formal algebra preserves an alternating product

The detector uses a super Frobenius algebra, a multiplication-and-pairing structure with even and odd parts. Odd coefficients anticommute, as in an exterior algebra. There is an independent odd generator θijk\theta_{ijk}θijk​ for each color triple.

The manuscript checks the graph identities needed to annihilate Pixton’s full original span, including the relevant boundary and forgetting operations. The test of YYY retains a nonzero coefficient proportional to the product of the distinct θijk\theta_{ijk}θijk​. This supplies the claimed formal nonmembership.

The detector is not asserted to be the actual Chow theory of a family of curves. That distinction is exactly what allows it to separate the original relation system from the additional geometric identity.

Actual curve correspondences obey a further vanishing law

On the geometric side, the small diagonal of a curve links three point positions. Projecting to the appropriate odd part of the curve’s correspondence structure produces a modified diagonal of the Gross–Schoen type, with corrections needed in families.

M1 studies quotient-sheaf moduli spaces on the square of the curve. Virtual localization and a Hilbert-scheme recursion retain marked outputs rather than integrating everything to a scalar. The resulting relation is intended to force sufficiently long products of the cubic coefficients to vanish in relative Chow theory.

Passing to the stable compactification introduces boundary errors. The rational-bridge correction with coefficient −1/2-1/2−1/2 removes a designated local error. The remaining terms either involve simpler operations or are supported over subsets of smaller dimension in the base.

An induction repeatedly pushes that support into higher codimension. The enormous color budget leaves enough marked inputs for each step until no support remains. This is the claimed Chow vanishing of YYY. The argument retains arbitrary Chow correspondences; replacing them with their cohomology classes would only establish a weaker result.

7. Scope, limitations, and open questions

The target is Pixton’s original relation system with its specified full formal closure, not a deliberately weakened selection of seed relations. The manuscript does not claim that any enlarged relation system is incomplete.

The example lives on M‾g,n\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}Mg,n​ at the displayed enormous parameters. It does not supply a small-genus counterexample, determine the first failure, or automatically disprove every completeness statement on the smooth unpointed or compact-type loci.

It also does not invalidate the known Pixton relations or establish that every non-Gorenstein phenomenon arises from a missing relation. Completeness, validity, and nondegeneracy of multiplication pairings are separate questions.

The remaining program would be to identify smaller examples, understand which additional relations are required, and formulate a replacement completeness conjecture with a geometric explanation for the new identities.

8. Sources and further reading

M1’s Definition 2.3 specifies the alternating class; Theorem 1.1 gives Chow vanishing and formal nonmembership; Corollary 1.2 gives the rational-cohomological consequence. Its introduction distinguishes the two proof mechanisms and the nearby Gorenstein questions.

The primary sources linked in Section 3 explain the original graph relations and their established validity. Optional background on tautological rings and moduli of algebraic curves can help with the vocabulary. The essential algebraic question is whether a known relation subspace equals the full kernel of geometric realization.

Source manuscripts

  • M1. OpenAI, A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow (September 24, 2026).

Sources consulted on 12 October 2026 at repository revision fd4aeeb. Download the manuscript citations.

entry.title: Family 054 — K3 structures without rationality for cubic fourfolds
entry.content:
← All digests

Family 054 · Algebraic and complex geometry
Importance 5/5 · Provisional editorial rating
Sources consulted 2026-10-12

1. The question

A polynomial equation can define a space whose points nevertheless admit a rational parametrization.
